articles.title: 2027: um ano de ajustes para a economia e o consumo brasileiro
articles.titleKo: 2027: um ano de ajustes para a economia e o consumo brasileiro
articles.originalSummary: Com a proximidade do fim de 2026, o cenário econômico para o próximo ano começa a ficar mais claro e as perspectivas são desafiadoras. As projeções de crescimento do PIB estão sendo revisadas para baixo , as expectativas de inflação voltaram a subir e a possibilidade de redução dos juros ficou mais distante. Mas é importante entender que esse cenário não surgiu agora. Independentemente do resultado eleitoral, 2027 já se desenhava como um ano de ajustes . Parte do crescimento que vimos em 2026 foi sustentado por uma injeção relevante de recursos na economia, seja por meio de programas de crédito, estímulos ao consumo ou medidas de transferência de renda. Esse impulso tende a perder força, enquanto os problemas estruturais que limitam o consumo continuam sendo o fiel da balança para um crescimento de longo prazo no país. Para o varejo, a indústria e os serviços, o desafio será operar em um ambiente de crescimento mais moderado, com um consumidor bastante pressionado e menos espaço para contar com estímulos econômicos. Cenário econômico mais restritivo As expectativas do mercado mostram uma mudança importante na perspectiva para 2027. As projeções para o próximo ano ainda estão sendo refeitas, mas, de forma geral, apontam para uma diminuição do crescimento do PIB, enquanto as estimativas de inflação e juros pioraram. No levantamento do Focus de 13/11/2026, do Banco Central, a expectativa de crescimento econômico para 2027 já caiu de 1,32% para 1,02% e a inflação saiu de 4,32% para 5,0%, a taxa de juros no fim de 2027 aumentou de 12% para 12,75%. É importante reforçar que o boletim Focus leva algum tempo para refletir em seus números as atualizações efetivas das projeções feitas pelos agentes econômicos, ou seja, esses números devem apresentar uma piora relevante nas próximas semanas. Esse conjunto de indicadores aponta para uma economia que deve crescer menos e conviver com condições financeiras restritivas por mais tempo. A inflação merece atenção especial, pois a alta acumulada dos preços continua corroendo o poder de compra das famílias. O consumidor não sente apenas a inflação do mês, mas também o efeito acumulado de anos de aumentos em alimentação, moradia, serviços, saúde e outras despesas essenciais desde o período pós-pandemia, em 2022, até agora. Além disso, juros elevados encarecem o crédito, dificultam novos financiamentos e aumentam o custo das dívidas existentes, colocado forte pressão sobre as empresas, que têm de capital mais elevados, maior pressão sobre o caixa e menor disposição para investimentos. O consumo continuará pressionado pelo orçamento das famílias Um dos principais desafios para 2027 está na situação financeira dos consumidores. O endividamento das famílias permanece elevado, e uma parcela cada vez maior da renda está comprometida com o pagamento de dívidas. O mapa da inadimplência do Serasa continua mostrando crescimento do número de brasileiros que estão com dívidas em atraso, somando 84,6 milhões de pessoas em outubro de 2026. Esse cenário limita a capacidade de consumo mesmo quando há renda disponível. Uma parcela relevante do dinheiro que poderia ser direcionada ao varejo acaba comprometida com juros, parcelas e renegociação de dívidas. Outro fator importante é a mudança na distribuição do orçamento. Com as despesas essenciais mais caras, as famílias precisam fazer escolhas priorizando alimentação, moradia, transporte e saúde. O resultado é uma redução do espaço para categorias mais discricionárias, como vestuário, móveis, eletrodomésticos, lazer e serviços. Portanto, não basta olhar para o crescimento da renda ou para a evolução do emprego. É preciso entender quanto efetivamente sobra no orçamento depois de pagar as despesas e compromissos financeiros. O mercado de trabalho é um importante ponto positivo Apesar dos desafios, a economia brasileira ainda conta com o mercado de trabalho aquecido. articles.title: Cheirin Bão abre primeira loja nos EUA e projeta 40 unidades no país em cinco anos
articles.titleKo: Cheirin Bão abre primeira loja nos EUA e projeta 40 unidades no país em cinco anos
articles.originalSummary: A rede de cafeterias Cheirin Bão inaugurou sua primeira unidade nos Estados Unidos, dando início à sua expansão internacional. A empresa investiu US$ 350 mil no projeto, montante que cobre taxa de franquia, reforma do imóvel, equipamentos e estruturação da operação, e projeta abrir 40 lojas no mercado norte-americano nos próximos cinco anos. A unidade, localizada em Ashland, Massachusetts, na região metropolitana de Boston, será administrada por parceiros locais, com suporte da Universal Franchising em áreas como treinamento, desenvolvimento de produtos, identidade visual e padronização de processos. “Construímos uma marca com forte identidade brasileira, baseada em cafés especiais e em uma experiência afetiva, e agora queremos mostrar que esse conceito também pode ganhar espaço fora do país”, afirma Wilton Bezerra, CEO e sócio-fundador da Cheirin Bão. O cardápio reúne referências da gastronomia mineira e produtos já conhecidos do consumidor norte-americano. Entre as opções estão os cafés especiais Bão, Mió e Moca, preparados por diferentes métodos, além de pão de queijo, coxinha, waffle de pão de queijo e hot dog com linguiça ao estilo mineiro. A carta inclui ainda cappuccinos, chocolate quente, bebidas geladas, donuts, brownies, cheesecakes, bolos e croissants. As receitas próprias da marca, como Banowaffle, Pãozinho de Chuva, Chocomallow, Uai Protein e Cappuccinoca, também fazem parte do cardápio. O abastecimento seguirá um modelo híbrido. Os cafés especiais, originários do Sul de Minas Gerais, serão torrados e enviados do Brasil aos Estados Unidos, assim como produtos como o chocolate em pó Chocobão, o cappuccino da marca e insumos específicos de empório. Os grãos também serão comercializados em embalagens de 250 gramas, destinadas ao preparo em casa. Expansão nos Estados Unidos mira Costa Leste A estreia ocorre em um momento de expansão da categoria nos Estados Unidos. Segundo o relatório National Coffee Data Trends 2026 , divulgado em junho pela National Coffee Association em colaboração com a Specialty Coffee Association, 47% dos adultos norte-americanos haviam consumido café especial no dia anterior à entrevista, ante 42% que tomaram café tradicional. Entre os consumidores de cafés especiais, 36% tomaram bebidas preparadas fora de casa, enquanto esse percentual foi de 23% entre os consumidores de café tradicional. Além de Ashland, a expansão está inicialmente concentrada na Costa Leste, com interesse em mercados como Flórida, Nova Jersey e Nova York. A marca já recebeu manifestações de interesse de potenciais parceiros nessas regiões, mas ainda não confirmou novos endereços ou datas de inauguração. No Brasil, a Cheirin Bão encerrou 2025 com faturamento de aproximadamente R$ 442 milhões, crescimento de 10,5% em relação ao ano anterior. Para 2026, a rede projeta alcançar R$ 550 milhões em receita. Atualmente, a marca conta com mais de 600 lojas, distribuídas por mais de 300 cidades e presente em todos os Estados brasileiros. Imagem: Divulgação O post Cheirin Bão abre primeira loja nos EUA e projeta 40 unidades no país em cinco anos apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: The New Playbook for Hotel & Resort Dining, According to Five F&B Leaders
articles.titleKo: The New Playbook for Hotel & Resort Dining, According to Five F&B Leaders
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Will guests remember the experience they had at your restaurant? That’s what will separate the next generation of hotel and resort dining concepts, whether it’s searing steak tableside or hosting events in collaboration with local artists. Here are five hotel and resort culinary leaders who are doubling down on high-touch hospitality and community engagement to create those memorable moments for guests. Ernie Brown Area Director of Culinary Operations Saint John’s Resort (Plymouth, Michigan) and The Inn at Stonecliffe (Mackinac Island) Ernie Brown When Ernie Brown took the culinary helm of two of Michigan’s leading resorts in April, one of his first priorities was refining each restaurant’s identity and creating distinctive, elevated dining experiences across each culinary concept. The James Beard Award-nominated chef brings more than 30 years of experience to his new role, with past stops at Caesars Palace, House of Blues, Nemacolin, Hotel Maverick, and Grand Hyatt Vail. One key piece of the puzzle for Brown was understanding how Saint John’s Resort and The Inn at Stonecliffe are both Humanitarian Hotels, where 100 percent of profit supports charitable initiatives around the world. It’s part of what attracted Brown to the opportunity, and that framework informs how he leads operations across the six dining concepts, as well as events and banquets, which are cornerstones of both properties’ businesses. “That really drew me to the property—just doing good for the community as well, not just working for another company that’s just putting money back in their pockets and feeding the billionaires,” Brown says. “We’re actually giving everything that we profit at the end of the day back to the community, back to the charitable foundation, and they donate that money to do great things.” At Saint John’s Resort, his impact is already underway, where he is reenvisioning the dining experiences across the resort’s concepts including FIVE Steakhouse, Doyles Irish Pub, and The Wine Grotto. At FIVE Steakhouse, he’s introducing new, immersive dining moments, like “The Cardinal,” an in-house dry-aged porterhouse for two carved tableside and finished with infused tallow butter. “We really wanted to focus on the steakhouse aspect,” Brown notes. Diners today—no matter if it’s at a standalone or hotel restaurant—want a visually striking, memorable experience, so even seemingly “simple” dishes must be presented in an exciting, theatrical way to deliver that “wow” factor and set the concept apart from a standard chain steakhouse, he argues. “That’s what people are looking for these days … They want to come somewhere that’s going to create an experience for them and their group.” That philosophy is showcased perfectly with the new Japanese A5 wagyu offering Brown introduced. Servers slice and sear the steak on a hot rock tableside, then place the seared steak into a housemade bao bun and top it with kimchi slaw and ponzu sauce. At FIVE Steakhouse, Ernie Brown is introducing new, immersive dining moments, like “The Cardinal,” an in-house dry-aged porterhouse for two carved tableside and finished with infused tallow butter. “It’s cooked right there in front of you, the server does everything for you,” Brown says. “It creates that atmosphere and that really cool feeling of ‘Oh, it’s tableside service and it’s very high-quality beef and it’s just a really cool experience.’ And we try to really drive that in with every course that we’re doing.” Before Brown arrived, none of the F&B concepts at either hotel were doing anything tableside. It took him a month and a half to roll the new menu out, which has received “great reviews so far,” he notes. “We’ve really elevated that service piece moving forward, and we’re going to continue to do that,” he adds. articles.title: How Justin Draper Feeds the Fantasy for Dellshire Resort Diners

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Justin Draper is feeding the fantasy for guests at Dellshire Resort, where he balances elevated dishes in a medieval setting—without being themed to the point of being tacky or garish. Yes, there may be a giant 70-foot fire-breathing dragon named Golspar at the entrance, but that doesn’t mean the dining experiences inside the six distinct venues aren’t elevated and culinary-driven. The first-of-its-kind resort opened this spring in Wisconsin Dells as one of the region’s most highly anticipated new hospitality destinations, blending medieval fantasy-inspired storytelling with the refined style of an upscale Midwestern retreat. Visitors step inside the two-story entrance framed by cathedral windows to find a castle brought to life, with stone masonry and sculptural corbels transporting them to a different time. As culinary director at Dellshire Resort, Justin Draper oversees all food and beverage venues both on- and off-site. A third-generation Wisconsin Dells chef, Draper took up the mantle following his role as executive chef and co-culinary director at Dawn Manor, which is now part of the Dellshire Resort collection. Located just minutes down the road, Dawn Manor is housed in a restored 19th century mansion overlooking Mirror Lake. The classy supper club has five period-themed private dining rooms, plus a downstairs speakeasy offering Prohibition-era cocktails and live entertainment. Draper oversees all food and beverage venues both on- and off-site, working closely with chefs to develop menus, guide kitchen teams, and ensure that each outlet delivers creativity, consistency, and a lasting experience for every guest. “The neat thing is that we have a zone or an experience for any occasion,” Draper says. “Dining is designed to feel like part of the adventure inside of Dellshire. We use imaginative concepts, presenting and storytelling to create that memorable experience.” The culinary program at Dellshire is anchored by the signature restaurant Blade & Barrel, featuring Wisconsin classics, alongside The Thirsty Dragon, a cozy fireside lounge; Scale Cove at Serpent’s Bay, a poolside swim-up bar; Kettle & Keep, a café and marketplace; and Gilded Spouts, located within the resort’s entertainment hub, Hero’s Hall. Each concept, from tavern-style dining to cocktails and hidden speakeasy moments, is designed to deepen the sense of exploration for guests. Draper is one of five F&B leaders featured in our November cover story, “The Next Wave of Hotel & Resort Restaurants.” Read the rest of the feature HERE . From thoughtfully crafted entrées to Wisconsin staples built on farm-forward ingredients, Blade & Barrel is designed to provide comfort while still having enough flair to intrigue the “adventurer.” For Draper, the challenge has been stepping outside of his comfort zone and updating his knowledge of the continually evolving nature of what guests want. Twenty‑five years ago, a simple turkey wrap with cheese, lettuce, and a mayo packet was a local hit; today, food trends have shifted, so he leans on younger team members to stay current. At Dellshire Castle, Draper is channeling that evolution into playful, story-driven, interactive dishes. At Blade & Barrel, for example, guests get to choose their own “sword” or blade when ordering a steak; servers present a magnetic board of around eight different steak knives for them to choose from. “I don’t want this too heavily themed because I want it to be approachable by everybody, but it’s hard not to notice it and then appreciate it while you’re here because it is all very top-end stuff that we’re doing. Your steak knife isn’t going to bend,” Draper says. articles.originalSummary: A Sodexo vai reforçar as equipes dos restaurantes que atendem em centros logísticos, oferecer refeições na madrugada e adaptar os cardápios durante a Black Friday. A empresa estima um aumento de cerca de 30% nas operações, acompanhando o aumento da demanda de empresas de comércio eletrônico e marketplaces. Na madrugada da virada da Black Friday, a companhia terá atendimento no formato conhecido como “corujão”, com equipes adaptadas aos horários de maior movimento. O atendimento especial começa nos dias que antecedem a data e continua depois da sexta-feira de promoções, quando o volume de trabalho nos centros de distribuição ainda é elevado. “Em um centro logístico, o tempo que um consumidor passa na fila do restaurante reflete diretamente no tempo que ele terá para descansar. Nossa entrega precisa acompanhar o aumento do volume e garantir a experiência, com abastecimento contínuo e agilidade no atendimento”, afirma Nathalie Camacho, diretora de Operações de E-commerce da Sodexo. A Sodexo prevê ainda a distribuição automatizada de bebidas quentes e o uso de insumos prontos para consumo, que dispensam etapas de preparo. Os cardápios levam em conta a rotina dos trabalhadores dos centros logísticos, muitos dos quais passam boa parte do expediente caminhando pelos galpões. “Nosso trabalho começa antes de o pico chegar ao restaurante. Precisamos antecipar demandas, propor soluções e organizar o atendimento para que a alimentação seja um momento de cuidado e descanso, mesmo nos dias mais intensos”, conclui a Nathalie A companhia criou uma diretoria dedicada ao atendimento de empresas de e-commerce e marketplaces. A nova área reúne equipes especializadas para atender às variações de demanda do setor, que costuma ter picos em campanhas de datas duplas, Black Friday e Natal. articles.title: Veja como será o cálculo da hora extra com a escala de trabalho 5×2
articles.titleKo: Veja como será o cálculo da hora extra com a escala de trabalho 5×2
articles.originalSummary: O ministro do Trabalho e Emprego, Luiz Marinho, explicou, nesta quinta-feira, 19, que a gradual redução da jornada semanal de trabalho e a garantia de dois dias de descanso remunerado vão elevar o valor da hora trabalhada, aumentando o custo das horas extras, mesmo que sem alterar os valores dos salários fixos mensais. Segundo Marinho, o decreto que regulamenta a nova escala de trabalho altera o cálculo usado para definir quanto vale cada hora de serviço. Com o decreto assinado hoje pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a escala passará a ser de cinco dias de jornada semanal por dois dias de descanso e haverá redução do atual limite semanal de 44 horas para 42 horas, a partir de 16 de dezembro deste ano, e para 40 horas, a partir de dezembro de 2027. Como o trabalhador receberá o mesmo salário por uma carga horária mensal menor, o valor de referência da hora sobe. Consequentemente, eleva o custo das horas extras e de outros adicionais trabalhistas. “Hoje, com a atual jornada de 44 horas, utilizamos, normalmente, um divisor [para calcular o valor da hora] equivalente a 220. Com [a entrada em vigor das] 42 horas, usaremos o divisor 210. E com 40 horas, 200. Isso significa que um trabalhador que recebe R$ 3 mil continuará recebendo a mesma quantia, mas o valor de referência de sua hora de trabalho passará a ser, a partir de 16 de dezembro, de R$ 14,29, e não mais os atuais R$ 13,64. E que, em dezembro de 2027, ela passará para R$ 15”, detalhou o ministro. Segundo ele, as empresas que preferirem evitar o impacto financeiro deverão contratar mais pessoal. “É só não convocar hora extra, substituindo-a por contratações”, disse Marinho durante a cerimônia de assinatura, pelo presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, do decreto que regulamenta a nova jornada de trabalho. Durante o evento, Marinho ainda buscou tranquilizar empregadores e consumidores, garantindo que o fim da escala 6×1 não significa o fechamento de estabelecimentos comerciais, restaurantes, hospitais ou indústrias aos sábados e domingos. Segundo Marinho, o decreto não restringe o funcionamento das atividades econômicas — inclusive daquelas que operam 24 horas por dia, durante todo o ano —, mas exige a reorganização das escalas de revezamento para assegurar as duas folgas semanais a cada funcionário. “Haveremos de orientar a atividade econômica que precisar trabalhar 365 dias por ano, 24 horas por dia, encaixando as escalas para dar conta da atividade. Além disso, a negociação coletiva poderá organizar a distribuição dos repousos ao longo do mês, respeitando duas folgas semanais e o descanso mínimo assegurado pela Constituição Federal”, assegurou Marinho. O minsitro destacou que a legislação aprovada estabelece flexibilidade para as empresas que, por suas características, não têm como garantir a seus empregados duas folgas em uma só semana. “Esta, contudo, não é a regra geral, que é de duas folgas semanais”, disse Marinho, ressaltando que os acordos e convenções coletivas vigentes permanecem válidos, e que só as cláusulas incompatíveis com os novos limites de jornada e de descanso perderão o efeito a partir de 16 de dezembro. Segundo Marinho, o decreto assinado nesta quinta-feira preserva os pisos salariais das categorias e alcança os trabalhadores urbanos, rurais e, no que couber, os avulsos. Ele ainda destacou que quem já trabalha 40 horas semanais ou menos, distribuídas por seis dias de trabalho e um de folga, também passará a ter direito garantido aos dois dias de repouso semanal remunerado. “A redução da jornada e a ampliação do descanso são direitos distintos e ambos precisam ser respeitados”, declarou Marinho, destacando que, em nenhum caso, pode haver redução salarial. Regimes especiais O decreto também estabelece regras para os regimes especiais de trabalho. A escala 12×36, utilizada em hospitais, serviços de vigilância, entre outras atividades, por exemplo, não será extinta, mas deverá observar os novos limites de jornada e os ajustes e compensaç

articles.title: Brasileiros aceitam IA para comparar preços, mas só 7% dispensam aprovação no pagamento
articles.titleKo: Brasileiros aceitam IA para comparar preços, mas só 7% dispensam aprovação no pagamento
articles.originalSummary: A maioria dos brasileiros está disposta a deixar a Inteligência Artificial (IA) realizar as buscas de preços nas compras de fim de ano, mas ainda resiste a dar à tecnologia a palavra final no pagamento. Segundo pesquisa da Visa realizada pela Morning Consult, 85% deixariam um agente de IA comparar preços, 82% permitiriam que ele verificasse a disponibilidade de produtos e 81% pediriam que resumisse informações ou avaliações. Quando se trata de concluir e pagar uma compra, porém, a disposição cai para 40%, e apenas 7% aceitariam que a IA fizesse isso sem aprovação prévia. O levantamento também indica que 73% dos brasileiros querem saber quando estão interagindo com um agente de IA. Para 48%, a ajuda da tecnologia nas compras de presentes ficou mais confortável do que no ano passado, ante quase um quarto dos adultos nos Estados Unidos. Além disso, 55% consideram provável usar IA para buscar ideias de presentes neste fim de ano, embora amigos e familiares continuem sendo a principal fonte de sugestões (41%), contra 14% que citam ferramentas de IA. “Os brasileiros incorporaram os pagamentos digitais ao dia a dia e agora demonstram a mesma abertura em relação à IA. Eles estão dispostos a deixar a IA pesquisar, comparar e sugerir, mas querem manter o controle na hora de pagar”, afirmou o presidente da Visa do Brasil, Rodrigo Cury. Online na frente Dois terços dos entrevistados (67%) esperam comprar presentes por canais online, acima dos 58% que planejam ir a lojas físicas. Outros 39% pretendem comprar ao menos um presente de vendedor de fora do País, e o preço mais baixo foi o principal motivo citado (44%). Uma viagem ou experiência de viagem aparece como o presente mais desejado depois de dinheiro, citada por 77%. Ainda assim, 37% disseram priorizar itens físicos neste ano, ante 15% que priorizam experiências. A Copa do Mundo de 2026 elevou o interesse por presentes ligados a esportes para 34% dos consumidores. Atrás das pechinchas Do lado dos custos, 92% dos brasileiros fizeram ao menos uma mudança no último ano para lidar com a alta das despesas do dia a dia, e a busca por descontos foi a medida mais comum (59%). Entre os que vão comprar presentes, metade planeja gastar menos de R$ 500. O relatório da Visa Business and Economic Insights (VBEI) aponta que o consumo nominal das famílias cresceu 6% no primeiro semestre de 2026 ante igual período do ano anterior. “O Brasil se destaca porque os consumidores se beneficiam tanto do crescimento real dos salários quanto da criação de empregos”, disse o economista para América Latina e Caribe da VBEI, Joel Virgen Rojano. Segundo ele, a temporada pode ser menos sobre se os consumidores vão gastar e mais sobre onde, quando e como. A pesquisa ouviu 1.045 adultos no Brasil, online, entre 26 de setembro e 5 de outubro de 2026, com margem de erro de 3 pontos porcentuais, para mais ou para menos. Rick Mijares remembers getting on his bike with neighborhood friends, heading to the local pizza shop for a slice, and dropping a few quarters into a video game. A trip to Sam Goody might follow. When the streetlights came on, it was time to head home. Those memories are the starting point for Pie Fidelity Pizza and Playlists, a new restaurant concept from the founder and managing partner of American Social Bar and Kitchen. The idea pairs New York-style pizza with an ’80s- and ’90s-inspired setting, drawing on the places where Mijares spent time before making plans meant reaching for a smartphone. He wants guests to recognize something of their own lives in it, too. For his generation, that might mean remembering afternoons spent riding around with friends. Older guests might recognize the neighborhood pizza shop where they took their children after baseball games—just as Mijares’ own parents did when he and his teammates were kids. “The kids all had clay on their pants and they ran around,” he says on FSR’s The Restaurant Innovator podcast. “I’m surprised the owner didn’t throw us out because there were kids everywhere and they were throwing garlic knots all over the place.” He adds one caveat for the guests who will make those memories at Pie Fidelity. “Hopefully they don’t do that.” Mijares opened his first American Social in June 2012, a 116-seat restaurant on Las Olas Boulevard in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. He had bartended in college, wanted to own a business, and saw an opportunity to combine his creative interests with an industry he enjoyed. A friend was franchising World of Beer, but Mijares wanted the freedom to develop something of his own. American Social brought together craft beer, a full bar, food, music, and sports. The first restaurant outperformed his highest projections, and within about six months, the conversation turned to opening another. A waterfront location in Miami’s Brickell neighborhood followed in 2014. Today, American Social spans five locations, with a sixth in development in Delray Beach. Pie Fidelity is being developed there, too, although a potential South Tampa restaurant could introduce the pizza concept first. A letter of intent is out for that location, Mijares says, and the condition of the space could allow it to move faster. The pizza will anchor the restaurant. But the experience around it is meant to give people a reason to settle in together while offering younger guests a glimpse of the places their parents have described. That vision took shape before the name did. Mijares initially called the concept Rick and Johnny’s. He liked the rhythm of it and could picture the neon colors, drawing on references like Miami Vice. What he couldn’t find was a meaningful connection between the name and the restaurant he wanted to create. “Ultimately, I couldn’t put a story behind the name,” he says. He approached a branding agency he had worked with on American Social and received a proposal that included naming the concept. But the prospect of handing over that responsibility bothered him. The restaurant came from his memories. He wanted its identity to come from him, too. “I wouldn’t accept the fact that I was gonna build a brand with a name not created by me,” Mijares says. Pie Fidelity, a play on “high fidelity,” connected the pieces: pizza, music, and the childhood experiences behind the concept. “I’m a music guy, I’m creative, I love Hi-Fi, I love those ’80s and ’90s movies,” he says. “They’ve influenced my life.” For Mijares, a name change was familiar territory. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Urban Plates has 22 locations. Urban Plates has figured out how to make a complicated restaurant business look surprisingly simple. Behind the scenes, the California fast casual prepares its food from scratch, serves customers across multiple channels, and offers a menu that stretches from nutrient-dense meals to burgers and chicken tenders. The result is a $4.5 million AUV. Fifteen years after opening its first location in Del Mar, Urban Plates has grown to 22 restaurants across California, with locations in San Diego, Orange County, Los Angeles, and Northern California. Now, cofounder Saad Nadhir is preparing to take the concept outside its home state again, armed with lessons from the pandemic and a model that has evolved considerably since 2011. Urban Plates previously operated three restaurants in the Washington, D.C., area as part of a national expansion plan. COVID interrupted those ambitions, prompting the company to exit the market and concentrate on California, where it had established infrastructure and operational expertise. Over the past year, Urban Plates has conducted a nationwide market analysis to identify cities with customer demographics and economic characteristics similar to those of its most successful California restaurants. The company expects to select one to three metropolitan markets outside California over the coming 12 months, although Nadhir has not disclosed specific locations or opening dates. “We think the concept is absolutely portable outside of California,” Nadhir says. “So the question is, can you get the volumes? And what are your operating costs outside of California? So we’re going through that analysis right now.” The expansion plans follow a period of significant operational changes. When Urban Plates debuted, customers moved along a service line, selected food displayed in front of them, and carried their meals to tables. Dine-in accounted for approximately 70 percent of sales before the pandemic. COVID forced the company to rethink that model. Urban Plates switched to counter ordering with food delivered to tables and invested in kitchen display systems to coordinate orders from different channels. Today, dine-in represents approximately 40 percent of sales, delivery accounts for 30 percent, and the remainder comes from takeout and catering. Digital transactions account for more than half of the business. The shift required new systems to maintain accuracy, speed, and food quality across channels. Nadhir says the company’s delivery error rate is approximately 1.5 percent, a result he attributes to its operational investments. “We’ve had to alter our systems to be able to accommodate the inflow of orders along those segments, and then us being able to fulfill them efficiently,” he says. Despite those changes, Urban Plates has preserved the scratch-made preparation and hospitality that distinguish it from other fast-casual concepts. The chain’s menu is built to accommodate different dietary preferences without creating unnecessary complexity in the kitchen. Proteins such as steak, chicken, and fish appear across plates, sandwiches, and salads, allowing the company to offer variety without requiring entirely different ingredients for each dish. Small-batch cooking and consistent preparation methods help the company maintain quality across its high-volume restaurants. Urban Plates also draws from full-service dining expertise. President Joe O’Donnell previously oversaw the western U.S. for Ruth’s Chris Steak House, and culinary chief Jim Cannon held a senior culinary role with the steakhouse chain. articles.title: Black Friday se estende por novembro e chega a restaurantes, bares e turismo
articles.titleKo: Black Friday se estende por novembro e chega a restaurantes, bares e turismo
articles.originalSummary: A Black Friday já não se concentra apenas nas lojas e nos produtos tradicionalmente associados à data. Restaurantes, bares e empresas de turismo também passaram a registrar aumento nas vendas durante o período, enquanto as compras pela internet avançam em ritmo superior ao das lojas físicas. Quinze anos após chegar ao Brasil, em 2010, a data se transformou em uma temporada de ofertas que ocupa praticamente todo o mês de novembro. Segundo o estudo do Mastercard Economics Institute (MEI), em 2025, os gastos online cresceram mais do que as compras presenciais em oito dos nove segmentos analisados. Em Móveis e Artigos para Casa, as vendas pela internet avançaram 26,1%, enquanto as lojas físicas registraram queda de 5,4%. Em Joias, o comércio eletrônico teve alta de 41,7%, diante da estabilidade no varejo físico. A diferença também aparece em setores que tradicionalmente não tinham a Black Friday como uma data relevante no calendário comercial. Em Restaurantes e Bares, os gastos com pedidos digitais cresceram 69,2% em 2025, a maior alta percentual entre as categorias avaliadas. Já o movimento presencial na sexta-feira teve participação pouco acima da registrada em um dia comum. O levantamento considerou os 20 dias anteriores e os sete dias posteriores à Black Friday de 2025, incluindo o período de antecipação das ofertas e ações como a Cyber Monday. O turismo também passou a fazer parte do calendário promocional. Pelo terceiro ano consecutivo, os gastos com Hospedagem e com Companhias Aéreas e Agências de Viagem tiveram crescimento de dois dígitos: 12,8% e 11,3%, respectivamente. Nas reservas de hospedagem pela internet, a alta chegou a 22,3%. No caso de passagens aéreas e pacotes, as compras presenciais também ganharam participação no dia oficial da Black Friday. A fatia desses gastos passou de 6,1%, em 2022, para 8,1%, em 2025. Entre os segmentos tradicionais do varejo, Beleza e Cosméticos registrou crescimento de 18,8% em relação ao período equivalente de 2024. Vestuário avançou 13,9%. Já os postos de combustíveis não apresentaram impacto relevante da temporada promocional. Ofertas distribuídas ao longo do mês A concentração das compras na sexta-feira também vem diminuindo. No comércio eletrônico de Eletrônicos, a participação dos gastos realizados exclusivamente no dia oficial caiu de 18,4%, em 2022, para 12,5%, em 2025. Em Hospedagem online, a parcela recuou de 12,8% para 8,9% no mesmo intervalo. Apesar da menor concentração na sexta-feira, os dois segmentos registraram crescimento superior a 20% no total de gastos durante o período promocional de 2025. As empresas passaram a antecipar as campanhas e distribuir descontos e condições especiais por mais dias. Com isso, a sexta-feira continua sendo o ponto alto da temporada, mas divide a atenção dos consumidores com as ofertas realizadas nas semanas anteriores e posteriores. “O avanço do comércio eletrônico e a entrada de categorias de serviços mostram que a Black Friday amadureceu no Brasil”, afirma Gustavo Arruda, economista-chefe do Mastercard Economics Institute para América Latina e Caribe. Para 2026, a projeção da Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Cartões de Crédito e Serviços (Abecs), em parceria com o Datafolha, é de que a temporada movimente R$ 17 bilhões, crescimento de 13,2% em relação à estimativa para 2025. Imagem: Envato O post Black Friday se estende por novembro e chega a restaurantes, bares e turismo apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .
koreanSummary: A Black Friday já não se concentra apenas nas lojas e nos produtos tradicionalmente associados à data.
Restaurantes, bares e empresas de turismo também passaram a registrar aumento nas vendas durante o período, enquanto as compras pela internet avançam em ritmo superior ao das lojas físicas.
Quinze anos após chegar ao Brasil, em 2010, a data se transformou em uma temporada de ofertas que ocupa praticamente todo o mês de novembro.

articles.title: Cowboy Chicken Expands Virtual Concept SmackBird
articles.titleKo: Cowboy Chicken Expands Virtual Concept SmackBird
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Cowboy Chicken, known for its signature wood-fired rotisserie chicken and homestyle favorites, is turning up the heat with the continued expansion of SmackBird, its Nashville hot chicken delivery-kitchen concept. Now operating in 11 locations, SmackBird is gaining ground as a distinct brand within the Cowboy Chicken family, bringing bold flavors, customizable heat and convenient online ordering to guests. Unlike a traditional standalone restaurant, SmackBird operates as a delivery-first kitchen within participating Cowboy Chicken locations. Guests order exclusively online at smackbird.com, choosing local delivery within designated service areas or pickup inside a participating Cowboy Chicken restaurant. While the two brands share kitchen operations, SmackBird maintains its own menu, identity and online ordering experience. SmackBird recently launched inside Cowboy Chicken at 1020 W. Nolana Ave. in McAllen,Texas and is set to open the 12 th delivery area in December in Frisco, Texas. The expansion reflects Cowboy Chicken’s strategy to introduce new dining options through its existing restaurant kitchens while building awareness and accessibility for the SmackBird brand. “SmackBird introduces a completely different flavor experience while leveraging the culinary expertise and restaurant operations that have defined Cowboy Chicken for decades,” said Sean Kennedy, president and CEO of Cowboy Chicken. “We see great potential to reach new guests who love hot chicken and appreciate the convenience of ordering online. “We’re building on our momentum with a clear vision for expanding SmackBird’s reach, introducing the brand to new audiences and creating additional opportunities across our existing restaurant network,” continued Kennedy A Different Kind of Chicken Experience SmackBird specializes in hand-breaded jumbo chicken tenders, crispy wings and generously sized sandwiches, all prepared fresh to order. Its signature Nashville hot-style flavors let guests choose their preferred level of heat, ranging from NoSmack and LiteSmack to GoodSmack and HardSmack For serious spice enthusiasts, the HellSmack Tender Challenge delivers an additional level of fiery intensity, featuring Scorpion pepper and a secret ingredient. The menu also includes crispy fries, creamy coleslaw, white cheddar mac and cheese, and desserts such as banana pudding and peach crumble. While Cowboy Chicken remains rooted in its wood-fired rotisserie cooking tradition, SmackBird brings a distinctly different personality and menu to the table. The two concepts provide guests with more ways to enjoy chicken, whether they are craving the comfort of a rotisserie chicken family meal or the bold kick of hot chicken. Building on a Growing Restaurant Platform SmackBird’s expansion demonstrates how Cowboy Chicken is extending its culinary capabilities beyond its core menu. By operating within participating Cowboy Chicken kitchens, the concept can enter markets without requiring a separate traditional storefront The recent McAllen opening and upcoming Frisco location mark the next steps in the brand’s growth, with opportunities for additional expansion as Cowboy Chicken evaluates its restaurant network and market demand. Guests can explore the SmackBird menu, find participating locations and place orders for delivery or pickup at smackbird.com. Let’s Get Social: Follow SmackBird on Facebook and Instagram. Register: Join the Smack Chat email club for access to fiery promotions. Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop, is coming to New Hyde Park with a new shop opening Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 909 Hillside Avenue. Located in North Shore Commons at the corner of Hillside Avenue and Lakeville Road, the opening marks the brand’s debut on Long Island and the first location for franchise group Legendary Eats, which plans to open additional shops throughout Nassau, Suffolk and Queens. Situated near the Lake Success Shopping Center and New Hyde Park Plaza, the shop will offer a convenient new dining option for nearby residents, employees and families. The opening also marks the beginning of Legendary Eats’ plans to grow the brand’s presence across Long Island and the surrounding communities. Legendary Eats’ connection to Potbelly began when the group’s founder discovered the brand while attending college in the Midwest and became a regular guest. Now, the group is bringing the neighborhood sandwich shop experience home to Long Island. Leading day-to-day operations is General Manager Eddie Bucher, a lifelong Great Neck resident with more than a decade of restaurant industry experience across Long Island. “Having grown up in Great Neck, I know how important neighborhood businesses are to the communities they serve,” said Bucher. “We’re looking forward to welcoming our neighbors, getting to know the people who live and work nearby and creating a place they can count on for great food and friendly service. We can’t wait for this shop to become a familiar stop for the New Hyde Park community.” To celebrate the shop’s arrival, Potbelly will host a grand opening celebration on Friday, Dec. 11 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. featuring a ribbon-cutting ceremony, a prize wheel with opportunities to win Potbelly giveaways, games and additional festivities. The new shop will feature the brand’s signature lineup of oven-toasted sandwiches and wraps, fresh salads, hand-dipped shakes and freshly baked cookies. Regular operating hours will be 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Guests can dine in or order ahead for pickup through Potbelly.com or the Potbelly App. Catering and third-party delivery are also available. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where they can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. To sign up, visit www.potbelly.com/perks . For more information about the new Potbelly location, visit www.potbelly.com. articles.titleKo: Beyond Juicery + Eatery Opens First Hospital Location at Cleveland Clinic’s Flagship Campus
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Beyond Juicery + Eatery has opened its first hospital location at Cleveland Clinic ‘s flagship campus at 9500 Euclid Ave., expanding the fast-casual brand into a new setting as it continues building its footprint through franchise development. The opening marks Beyond Juicery + Eatery’s sixth new restaurant opening of 2026, bringing its total to 55 open locations. Following successful openings in Atlanta and Florida this year, and with its continued presence in Ohio, the brand expects to open another restaurant in Michigan before year-end, with several more in development for early 2027. Its expansion plans also include five South Florida restaurants through a franchise agreement with international music star and entrepreneur Flo Rida. “Opening at Cleveland Clinic is a natural next step for Beyond Juicery + Eatery and our long-standing commitment to food that makes you feel beyond good,” said Jasmine Miller, CEO of Beyond Juicery + Eatery. “We’re proud to bring fresh, flavorful food made on-site to a healthcare setting, where convenient options that taste great and make you feel good matter. We hope this is the first of many similar locations as we explore opportunities to bring our menu to more campuses and healthcare environments.” Franchisee Jason Chamoun, who owns multiple fast-casual brands and foodservice businesses, will lead the brand’s eighth currently operating location in Ohio. Through his existing partnership with Cleveland Clinic, Chamoun brings firsthand knowledge of the campus and the needs of its visitors, caregivers and employees. “People in a healthcare setting have busy days, and having access to a good meal without having to leave campus is important,” said Mijo Alanis, co-founder of Beyond Juicery + Eatery. “We’ve always believed that better-for-you options should be convenient without sacrificing flavor, and this location gives us an opportunity to put that belief into practice in a setting where people already have so much on their mind.” The restaurant serves made-to-order smoothies, wraps, salads, juices and breakfast items. A grab-and-go cooler stocked with organic, cold-pressed bottled juices offers an additional option for those on the move, while in-store kiosks and mobile ordering through the Beyond Juicery + Eatery app provide ordering flexibility. Beyond Juicery + Eatery began franchising in 2018 and continues to pursue development opportunities with operators who share its focus on fresh, functional and flavorful dining. With a strong pipeline of new restaurants in development, Beyond Juicery + Eatery is positioned for continued growth in 2027 and beyond. For more information and a full list of Beyond Juicery + Eatery locations, visit beyondjuiceryeatery.com or visit franchise.beyondjuiceryeatery.com to explore franchising opportunities. Chef Stephanie Izard, the James Beard Award winner behind Chicago’s Girl & the Goat, is bringing her globally inspired cooking to Miami with Ladygoat, a new restaurant opening in Wynwood in early 2027 in partnership with Miami’s award-winning restaurant group Grove Bay Hospitality Group. The restaurant marks the group’s ﬁrst collaboration with Izard. The homegrown restaurant group is known for its extensive portfolio of award-winning restaurants including Michelin-starred concept Stubborn Seed, helmed by Top Chef winner Jeremy Ford with locations in Miami Beach and Las Vegas; Coconut Grove’s waterfront dining destination Bayshore Club; Glass and Vine; and Michelin Guide recommended Beauty & The Butcher in Coral Gables. Izard will work closely alongside Grove Bay’s culinary team to bring her bold, globally inspired cooking to one of Miami’s most vibrant creative districts. The partnership pairs one of the country’s most celebrated chefs with a group that has helped shape Miami’s dining scene. “Miami has such a vibrant food scene, and Wynwood’s energy and creativity make it the perfect home for Ladygoat,” says Stephanie Izard. “I’m so excited to partner with the Grove Bay team, who know this city and its diners so well. Plus, the opportunity to work alongside my good chef friend, Kenny Gilbert, the VP of Culinary Operations for Grove Bay.” Ladygoat will be located at the former Rosemary’s space in Wynwood. The menu, set to debut with the restaurant’s opening in early 2027, will feature standout dishes such as a wood-ﬁred seafood tower featuring local catch; ﬂaky goat empanadas served with huacatay mayo; Girl & the Goat’s beloved sautéed green beans paired with ﬁsh sauce vinaigrette and cashews; a sticky crunchy pork shank alongside an assortment of sauces and pikliz made for sharing; and a wood ﬁred porterhouse ﬁnished with Castelvetrano olive chimichurri and miso garlic brown butter. Leading the kitchen at Ladygoat as Chef de Cuisine is Logan McNeil, a familiar face within the Grove Bay family. A Stubborn Seed alum, McNeil was a driving force behind the restaurant’s critically acclaimed menu and played a pivotal role in the restaurant earning its Michelin Green Star in 2025. Most recently, McNeil served as the Chef de Cuisine at Michelin-starred Tambourine Room by Tristan Brandt. Sustainability has long guided McNeil’s approach in the kitchen and will be central to the culinary program at Ladygoat with Izard. “I still remember visiting Girl & the Goat when it ﬁrst opened more than 15 years ago and loving everything about it,” says Ignacio Garcia-Menocal, CEO and co-founder of Grove Bay Hospitality Group. “Stephanie Izard is one of the most talented chefs in the country, and her food has a way of bringing people together. To partner with a chef I’ve admired for so long and bring her vision to our city is incredibly exciting – and we knew Ladygoat would be the perfect addition to Miami’s dining scene.” “I’ve admired Stephanie’s work since her earliest days, and I always knew we’d ﬁnd a way to work together here in Miami. When we started looking for the right concept for Wynwood, it felt like the moment had ﬁnally arrived. She brings a fresh energy that ﬁts the neighborhood perfectly,” says Francesco Balli, CEO and co-founder of Grove Bay Hospitality Group. Izard made history as the ﬁrst woman to win Bravo’s Top Chef , but her accolades stretch far beyond the hit TV show. The recipient of James Beard Best Chef: Great Lakes and Food & Wine Best New Chef, Izard won the coveted title of “Iron Chef” in 2017 and is the Executive Chef and Partner of Girl & the Goat, Little Goat, Duck Duck Goat, Cabra and Lucky Goat in Chicagoland, along with Girl & the Goat and Valley Goat in California and more. articles.title: Lucro líquido total do BNDES cresce 18% e soma R$ 20,3 bi nos primeiros 9 meses de 2026
articles.titleKo: Lucro líquido total do BNDES cresce 18% e soma R$ 20,3 bi nos primeiros 9 meses de 2026
articles.originalSummary: O Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) registrou lucro líquido recorrente de R$ 12,3 bilhões nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, um aumento de 10% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. Considerando os ganhos com vendas de ações registrados diretamente em lucros acumulados, o lucro líquido total somou R$ 20,3 bilhões, alta de 18% frente aos nove primeiros meses de 2025. A diferença entre o resultado recorrente e o lucro total foi impulsionada por efeitos não recorrentes líquidos de tributos. Entre eles, destacaram-se as receitas de dividendos e juros sobre o capital próprio (JCP), que somaram R$ 2,5 bilhões – principalmente de Petrobras e JBS. Também houve R$ 5 bilhões provenientes de vendas de ações, com destaque para Petrobras (R$ 3,6 bilhões) e Copel (R$ 1 bilhão), além de operações envolvendo Axia e Copasa. Outros efeitos não recorrentes responderam por R$ 500 milhões. Em setembro, a carteira de participações societárias do banco totalizou R$ 94,1 bilhões. As principais empresas investidas seguem sendo Petrobras, JBS, Axia e Copel. Durante a entrevista coletiva de apresentação dos resultados, o presidente do BNDES, Aloizio Mercadante, explicou que a venda de parte das ações da Petrobras ocorreu por uma obrigação regulatória. “Como houve uma valorização muito grande da Petrobras, principalmente com a guerra e o preço do petróleo, a ação passou muito dos 25% da nossa carteira. Então nós tínhamos obrigação regulatória de fazer uma venda. Nós aproveitamos o momento extraordinário da recorde das ações da empresa”, detalhou. O presidente do BNDES também classificou como uma “inovação importante” a operação realizada com os papéis da Axia. Em uma oferta de conversão promovida pela companhia, o banco vendeu ações preferenciais (PN) e comprou ações ordinárias (ON), gerando um ganho de R$ 50 milhões. “Criamos condições de participar do controle da empresa. É um valor ainda não muito expressivo, mas dentro de uma estratégia. Para nós foi um ótimo negócio, porque o preço da PN estava acima da ON. Então tivemos um ganho na operação e, além disso, ficamos com uma ação que nos interessa mais”, detalhou. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Paula Martini e Gabriela da Cunha). articles.title: ‘DOU’ Extra traz decreto de regulamentação do fim da 6×1, com cálculo da hora de trabalho
articles.titleKo: ‘DOU’ Extra traz decreto de regulamentação do fim da 6×1, com cálculo da hora de trabalho
articles.originalSummary: O governo do presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), publicou nesta quinta-feira, 19, em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União ( DOU ) , o decreto que regulamenta o fim da escala de trabalho 6×1. As disposições são aplicadas aos empregados urbanos, aos empregados rurais, aos empregados domésticos e, no que couber, aos trabalhadores avulsos. O texto traz o cálculo da hora de trabalho e também especificações para os empregados que trabalham em turnos ininterruptos e em jornadas de 12 horas. O decreto foi assinado na manhã desta quinta-feira pelo presidente reeleito, em cerimônia realizada no Palácio do Planalto. Estiveram presentes o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin; os ministros do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho, e da Secretaria Geral, Guilherme Boulos; o presidente do Tribunal Superior do Trabalho (TST), Luiz Philippe Vieira de Mello Filho; e representantes sindicais. Também estiveram presentes vários congressistas, entre eles o deputado Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG), autor da PEC que acabou sendo votada, o deputado André Janones (Rede-MG), e o líder do governo na Câmara, Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS). O vereador e deputado federal eleito Rick Azevedo (Psol-RJ), que começou o atual movimento de pressão pelo fim da escala 6×1 por meio do Movimento Vida Além do Trabalho (VAT), também participou do evento. A principal ausência foi da deputada Érika Hilton (Psol-SP), autora de uma das propostas de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que levaram à redução da jornada de trabalho. Segundo o decreto, para os empregados sujeitos à duração normal do trabalho, o salário-hora será calculado com base no divisor 210, para jornadas máximas de 42 horas semanais, e no divisor 200, para jornadas de até 40 horas semanais. O divisor é um parâmetro usado para calcular o valor da hora de trabalho a partir do salário mensal. O cálculo normal estabelece a multiplicação do total de horas trabalhadas por cinco (por isso as 42 horas semanais têm divisor de 210 e as 40 horas, de 200). Em discurso na cerimônia de assinatura do decreto, o ministro do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho, explicou que hoje, na jornada de 44 horas, é normalmente utilizado o divisor 220. “Isso significa que um trabalhador que recebe hoje R$ 3.000,00 continuará recebendo os mesmos R$ 3.000,00, mas o valor de referência de sua hora passará agora, em 16 de dezembro, de R$ 13,64 para R$ 14,29. Em dezembro de 2027, a hora passará para R$ 15,00”, exemplificou. “É uma mudança importante para o cálculo das horas extras e de outros direitos trabalhistas.” E afirmou: “Os empresários falam, poxa, mas vai impactar. É só não convocar hora extra, é só substituir por contratações que não terá nenhum impacto.” Esse cálculo, porém, não impede a aplicação de um divisor menor, desde que previsto em lei, convenção ou acordo coletivo de trabalho, ou decorrente de jornada contratual inferior à duração normal semanal. Segundo o decreto, deve prevalecer, “em qualquer hipótese”, o divisor mais favorável ao empregado. O decreto ainda determina que os empregados que trabalham em turnos ininterruptos de revezamento terão assegurada jornada de seis horas diárias, exceto se houver disposição diversa estabelecida em convenção ou acordo coletivo de trabalho. Deverá ser observado, no mês-calendário, a média de duração do trabalho correspondente ao limite semanal constitucional e o repouso semanal remunerado de dois dias. Por sua vez, os empregados que trabalham em jornadas de 12 horas consecutivas de trabalho por 36 horas ininterruptas de descanso terão a compensação das horas trabalhadas ou o pagamento de horas extras quando a jornada resultar, no mês-calendário, em média superior ao limite semanal constitucional, nos termos estabelecidos em convenção ou acordo coletivo de trabalho. A emenda à Constituição que acaba com a escala 6×1 foi promulgada em 16 de outubro pelo Congresso. A sessão contou com a participação do presidente Lula, que tinha na proposta uma de suas bandeiras à reeleição. A primeira etapa da emenda constitucional e
koreanSummary: O governo do presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), publicou nesta quinta-feira, 19, em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União ( DOU ) , o decreto que regulamenta o fim da escala de trabalho 6×1.
As disposições são aplicadas aos empregados urbanos, aos empregados rurais, aos empregados domésticos e, no que couber, aos trabalhadores avulsos.

articles.title: When Franchise Technology Becomes a Legal Liability
articles.titleKo: When Franchise Technology Becomes a Legal Liability
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A brand standard tells a franchisee what result the system expects: a clean store, a consistent product, a safe delivery. How to get there stays with the franchisee. A franchisee asks for help: a competitor down the road just adopted software that clocks workers in, prompts upsells, and reports every sale. The franchisor responds by rolling out its own version to every location. Years later, that software is the centerpiece of a lawsuit against the franchisee and the franchisor. In that case and ones like it, plaintiffs may call their theory joint employment, vicarious liability, or agency, but each asks the same question: did the franchisor stay within the minimum standards that protect its brand, or did its control reach the franchisee’s day-to-day operations? The answer often depends on the kind of control at issue, as a review of more than 600 franchise decisions issued since 2020, from motions to dismiss through trial, shows. When courts relied on allegations that a franchisor’s control went beyond enforcing brand standards, and those allegations did not involve technology, they treated those facts as evidence of impermissible control roughly a third of the time. When the allegations involved the franchisor’s technology platform—an allegation that has been observed to occur 3 times more often since 2020—that figure rose to more than half. Why Technology Is Different A brand standard tells a franchisee what result the system expects: a clean store, a consistent product, a safe delivery. How to get there stays with the franchisee. Software may implicitly take that choice away. It may clock in the crew, script the upsell, and keep a timestamped record of each step. In other words, it may perform the daily work that standards are supposed to leave to the operator and create evidence that it did. Massage Heights Franchising v. Hagman shows how far brand standards can go. There, the franchisor required franchisees to run background checks on massage therapists, controlled the draping method therapists used, specified their training, detailed how they should interact with clients, and set protocols for responding to sexual assault allegations. After a franchisee’s therapist allegedly assaulted a customer, a jury found the franchisor negligent. In 2025, the Texas Supreme Court reversed, finding that the franchisor’s alleged control was not enough for it to be held liable. Ronquillo v. Doctor’s Associates shows the opposite. A worker at a Subway franchise sued the Subway franchisor under Illinois’s biometric privacy law. She alleged that Subway’s point-of-sale software, which the franchisor “exclusively controls,” captured workers’ fingerprints when they clocked in. In 2022, a federal court in Chicago refused to let the franchisor put the collection solely on its franchisee, and the claim went forward. The difference between the two cases is not how much control the franchisor had. In Massage Heights , the franchisor set rules and left the work to the franchisee. In Ronquillo , the franchisor’s software did the work itself. Using Technology The Safest Way Courts have yet to decide whether a franchisor’s AI tool can make it liable for a franchisee’s workforce, and some assume that question will require a new analysis. It should not. The numerous decisions where franchisor technology was at issue provide plenty of guidance for how this analysis should proceed and what franchise systems can do to protect themselves: 1. Provide Technology to Aid, Not Dictate, Operations. A court held that requiring franchisees to use one brand of point-of-sale system did not make them a national coffee chain’s agents, because that control did not reach the system’s “functionality or operation.” Similarly, a pizza franchisor required drivers to use its delivery app, but a court held that a tool that “mechanically aids deliveries” is

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Salty, a national modern donut and coffee brand with more than 20 location across the U.S. known for its premium 24-hour brioche donuts and meticulously sourced coffee program, has entered the CPG space with the launch of its new bottled, clean-label syrups. Designed to bring The Salty coffee shop experience home, the inaugural collection features three signature syrups to infuse premium flavor to homemade lattes, cold brew, matcha and more. The Salty’s core collection includes: Salted Vanilla : Sweet, creamy vanilla with a subtle hint of salt for a smooth, balanced flavor that goes with just about anything Cinnamon Cereal: Warm, toasted cereal milk flavor with cinnamon spice and creamy sweetness for a nostalgic twist on your everyday coffee or matcha Maple & Brown Sugar : Deep, caramelized brown sugar blended with real maple syrup for a rich, cozy sweetness “From the beginning, we’ve believed that great flavor starts with great ingredients, and our house-made syrups are a natural extension of that philosophy,” said Amanda Pizarro, The Salty’s Founder and Chief Brand Officer. “Our customers have always looked for ways to recreate their favorite drinks at home, and we’ve made that possible without compromising on the quality, creativity or attention to detail that defines The Salty. These syrups will allow us to reach guests well beyond our shops and we hope to see The Salty become a part of more people’s daily coffee ritual.” True to The Salty’s brand ethos, the syrups are crafted with clean ingredients and without the use of artificial flavors, dyes or preservatives. Each eight-ounce recyclable glass bottle has approximately 10 servings and a shelf life of two-years unopened or six-months open and refrigerated. Flavors can be purchased individually ($16) or in a three-pack ($45) and are available at all Salty locations or online at saltydonut.com with nationwide shipping. In addition to its signature offerings, The Salty plans to release limited-edition seasonal flavors. Its fall collection includes Brown Sugar Pumpkin (real pumpkin, rich brown sugar and warm fall spices for a cozy sip) and Salted Hazelnut (rich, nutty hazelnut with a subtle hint of salt for smooth balanced sweetness). Deputing Nov. 27, the holiday collection will feature Apple Pie and Honey & Cardamom Bun. Founded by Amanda Pizarro and her then-boyfriend, now-husband Andy Rodriguez as a Miami pop-up in 2015, The Salty has since grown to more than 20 brick-and-mortar locations across eight states. The brand’s entrance into the CPG category comes on the heels of its rapid retail growth, opening eight of its locations since January 2025 and unveiling a new savory food menu at select stores. Deeply rooted in community and guest experience, The Salty has hosted high-profile brand collaborations including Poppi, Snif, Summer Fridays, Salt & Straw and MINI to bring immersive guest activations to its locations nationwide. For more information about The Salty, visit saltydonut.com. The post The Salty Enters CPG Space with Bottled Clean-Label Syrups appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Produtividade: estamos medindo e direcionando esforços corretamente?
articles.titleKo: Produtividade: estamos medindo e direcionando esforços corretamente?
articles.originalSummary: Produtividade é, diversas vezes, associada à quantidade de tarefas realizadas, ao volume de trabalho executado ou, simplesmente, ao número de horas que cada profissional permanece na empresa. Mas será que estar ocupado significa, necessariamente, ser produtivo? Essa é uma pergunta que empresários e lideranças precisam começar a fazer com mais frequência. Especialmente em um momento em que as margens estão pressionadas, os custos operacionais exigem atenção redobrada e o consumidor pensa cada vez mais antes de abrir a carteira. Segundo o IBGE, as vendas do comércio varejista brasileiro cresceram apenas 0,2% em setembro de 2026, na comparação com agosto. Já a Confederação Nacional do Comércio (CNC) apontou que 81,6% das famílias brasileiras estavam endividadas em outubro. Embora endividamento não signifique necessariamente inadimplência, o dado reforça a necessidade de compreender as limitações e prioridades do orçamento do consumidor. Nesse contexto, crescer não depende apenas de atrair mais clientes. Depende também de aproveitar melhor as oportunidades que já existem. Recentemente, ao discutir a transição da escala 6×1 para a 5×2, provoquei os empresários a repensar a distribuição de suas equipes antes de assumir novas contratações como única alternativa. Fernando Cardoso, sócio-diretor da Gouvêa Foodservice, deu continuidade à reflexão ao explorar as particularidades das operações de alimentação , demonstrando que o redesenho do trabalho envolve também processos, abastecimento, tecnologia e desenvolvimento de competências. Mas gostaria de avançar um pouco mais nessa conversa: o que estamos, de fato, considerando produtividade dentro das nossas empresas? Equipes ocupadas nem sempre são equipes produtivas Imagine uma loja de moda em que os vendedores passam boa parte do expediente organizando araras, conferindo etiquetas, movimentando mercadorias e realizando atividades administrativas. Todos parecem ocupados. Quantas oportunidades de atendimento e venda estão sendo perdidas enquanto essas tarefas são executadas? Em uma farmácia, os colaboradores podem dedicar tempo excessivo a processos manuais, conferências e atividades operacionais, enquanto clientes aguardam atendimento ou deixam de receber orientações e sugestões relevantes. Em um restaurante, a equipe pode trabalhar intensamente durante todo o expediente, mas enfrentar atrasos, retrabalho, desperdícios e dificuldades de comunicação entre cozinha e salão. Perceba que, nos três exemplos, não estamos necessariamente falando de falta de esforço ou comprometimento das pessoas, mas da forma como o trabalho foi organizado. Uma operação pode ter profissionais extremamente dedicados e, ainda assim, apresentar baixa produtividade. E esse é um dos principais equívocos da gestão: confundir intensidade de trabalho com geração de resultados. Estamos medindo o esforço ou o resultado? O varejo evoluiu muito no acompanhamento de indicadores: faturamento, ticket médio, conversão, itens por atendimento, margem e metas individuais fazem parte da rotina de inúmeras empresas. Mas quantas delas conseguem relacionar esses resultados à quantidade de horas efetivamente trabalhadas? A receita gerada por hora trabalhada, por exemplo, ajuda a compreender quanto a operação consegue produzir comercialmente com o tempo disponível. Vamos imaginar duas lojas com características semelhantes, ambas faturando R$ 300 mil mensais: A primeira utiliza 1.500 horas de trabalho no período. A segunda,1.200 horas. A primeira gera R$ 200 por hora trabalhada. A segunda, R$ 250. Ou seja, a segunda apresenta produtividade comercial por hora 25% superior. Mas atenção: Isso não significa, automaticamente, que seja mais rentável. Se a segunda loja trabalha com descontos excessivos, apresenta perdas elevadas ou compromete a experiência dos clientes, parte dessa aparente vantagem pode desaparecer. Por isso, não basta analisar apenas a receita por hora. É preciso relacioná-la também à margem, às despesas operacionais, à qualid

articles.title: Port of Subs Hits Major Franchise Milestone, Expands to Cuba
articles.titleKo: Port of Subs Hits Major Franchise Milestone, Expands to Cuba
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Port of Subs, the neighborhood sandwich franchise known for its fresh, made-to-order subs, closed out a milestone third quarter of franchise development, completing its founding “Twenty Club” of Regional Developers and signing four new Regional Developers in total. The brand also expanded to Cuba with a new location at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, earned a spot at No. 384 on the 2026 Franchise Times Top 400 , and has opened 11 new locations year-to-date, building momentum as it heads into the final quarter of the year. The Q3 results reflect Port of Subs’ deliberate growth strategy: partnering with experienced, entrepreneurial Regional Developers who serve as local extensions of the brand, leading franchise sales and providing long-term support to operators in their markets. Backed by more than 54 years in business and franchise growth engine Area 15 Ventures, the brand continues to expand across both traditional and non-traditional venues nationwide. Port of Subs Completes Its Founding “Twenty Club” In Q3, Port of Subs reached a key benchmark: completing the elite “Twenty Club” consisting of the founding 20 Regional Developers who will set the stage for the brand’s national expansion. The brand’s Regional Developer momentum didn’t stop there. Port of Subs went on to multiple additional Regional Developers during the quarter, extending its reach into new markets across the country: Regional Developer No. 22: Mitul Chothani and Hitesh Barvaliya will lead development of 10 locations across Fort Myers. Chothani and Barvaliya are successful multi-unit franchisees of several QSR brands across Florida. Regional Developer No. 23: Richard Wenschlag and Ed Kofol will lead development of nine locations across Boise. Wenschlag and Kofol are multi-unit owners and developers of a frozen yogurt brand. Each Regional Developer will lead franchise sales and support in their respective markets, identifying strong local operators and building out the brand’s neighborhood presence. Port of Subs provides Regional Developers and franchisees with real estate, operations, marketing, training and technology resources, along with a simplified operating model that requires no cooking or grills. From Guantanamo Bay to Sea-Tac: A Non-Traditional Push On the development front, Port of Subs has opened 11 new locations year-to-date through Q3, bringing its footprint to more than 129 locations across the U.S. The brand forged ahead with its push into more non-traditional venues throughout Q3, highlighted by the opening of a location at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay in Cuba, in partnership with the U.S. Navy. Located at the Navy’s oldest overseas base, the new store brings Port of Subs’ made-to-order subs to service members, their families and civilian personnel stationed on the island. The brand also opened a store at Naval Air Station Oceana, also in partnership with the Navy, as well as a location at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. “This quarter showed what’s possible when you pair a proven, simple model with the right local leaders,” said Healey Mendicino, President & CEO of Port of Subs. “Completing our Twenty Club was a milestone we’ve been building toward, and signing three more Regional Developers right behind it tells us the momentum is real. We’re entering the fourth quarter in a strong position to keep bringing Port of Subs to more neighborhoods across the country.” To learn more about franchising opportunities with Port of Subs, please visit www.franchising.portofsubs.com. articles.titleKo: Penn Station Signs Deal in Troy, Michigan
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Penn Station Sandwiches, the fast-casual sandwich franchise beloved for its grilled-to-order subs, fresh-cut fries, and hand-squeezed lemonade, is excited to announce expansion of the brand in Troy, Michigan. The newly signed development agreement was inked by mother-son team Brendan and Colleen Gumbel, marking the beginning of their family’s venture into franchise ownership with the brand. A Michigan native and 2022 graduate of Michigan State University, Brendan brings a background in supply chain management, purchasing and project management to the new business venture. His interest in Penn Station began with a personal connection to the brand: a cousin who owns two Penn Station restaurants in Michigan. After learning more about the franchise opportunity through his cousin and connecting with Penn Station’s development team, Brendan and Colleen began exploring what ownership could look like. Their conversations eventually led to a signed single-unit development agreement for Troy. “Having grown up with Penn Station just down the road, I’ve always loved the food and been familiar with the brand,” said Brendan Gumbel. “What really stood out to us was the people and the support behind the franchise. After meeting the corporate team and learning more about the business, we felt very comfortable moving forward. We’re excited about the opportunity to build something of our own with Penn Station.” Colleen, who lives in nearby Rochester Hills, is partnering with Brendan on the investment. The family plans to bring the brand to Troy, a market they believe offers strong potential given its mix of businesses, schools, retail destinations and established dining options. “We’re excited to welcome Brendan and Colleen to the Penn Station family as we continue to grow our franchise network in Michigan,” said Don Champion, vice president of sales and franchise development for Penn Station Sandwiches. “Our refreshed brand identity and expanded menu reflect the continued evolution of the brand and the opportunities ahead for new franchise owners. We look forward to supporting the Gumbels as they bring Penn Station’s signature sandwiches to Troy.” The Troy restaurant is currently targeted to open in 2027, with the specific site and construction timeline still being finalized. Founded more than 40 years ago, Penn Station Sandwiches has grown to more than 300 restaurants nationwide while maintaining a focus on quality ingredients, made-to-order food and operational excellence. The brand’s recent rebrand bringing an expanded menu for more occasions is part of a strategy that prioritizes sustainable growth, franchisee profitability, and market development opportunities for qualified operators like the Gumbels. Entrepreneurs interested in learning more about franchise opportunities with Penn Station can visit https://penn-station.com/franchise/ and join the conversation on Facebook https://www.facebook.com/pennstation and Instagram https://www.instagram.com/pennstationsandwiches/. Keith Lee built his following on honest reviews of other people’s food. Now, for the first time, he’s putting his name on a food product: meet the Keith Lee Pork Belly Fried Rice Dumpling , created in collaboration with Brooklyn Dumpling Shop . This week, Brooklyn Dumpling Shop launched its newest creation in partnership with creator, food critic, and Brooklyn Dumpling brand investor Keith Lee: the Keith Lee Pork Belly Fried Rice Dumpling. It’s smoky-sweet char siu pork belly and fried rice folded into a dumpling and available now across Brooklyn Dumpling Shop locations in New York, New Jersey, Philadelphia, Miami, and Dallas, including at the brand’s latest opening in DeKalb Market Hall in Brooklyn, New York. The launch marks Lee’s first-ever food product, featuring a flavor he developed with Brooklyn Dumpling Shop and his chef, Alexia Grant . The new dumpling was chosen by Lee’s fans following his taste test at Brooklyn Dumpling Shop’s Dallas, TX location, where he sampled four specially requested dumpling flavors and invited his audience to vote for their favorite . Famous for candid restaurant reviews and inspiring audiences to explore new dining experiences, Lee knew he wanted to create a dumpling that not only tasted delicious, but also brought the distinctiveness of the Brooklyn Dumpling Shop brand by putting a reimagined twist on a familiar dish. “We’re built on ‘Everything’s Better in a Dumpling™,’ and we nailed the beloved flavor of pork fried rice in our delicious way,” said Jeff Galletly, Chairman and CEO of Brooklyn Dumpling Shop. “It was a dream to co-create this product alongside Keith and his team. We’re all about highly craveable fusion flavors, and we’re proud to launch Keith’s first-ever food item as a memorable moment for our fans, shop team members, and our franchisees.” “Making this dumpling with Brooklyn Dumpling Shop has meant a lot to me. I wanted to ensure it’d be something I’d be proud to share with my community, and the team really got it just right,” said Keith Lee, creator and Brooklyn Dumpling Shop investor. “Bringing this vision to life has been an unforgettable experience and we knew our fans had to be involved in choosing the final dumpling, because y’all are the reason I get to do any of this. I’m so grateful and I really hope everyone enjoys it as much as we enjoyed making it for you.” The dumpling is available on the “ Keith Lee’s Faves ” menu in every U.S. Brooklyn Dumpling Shop location, including the latest opening at DeKalb Market Hall in Brooklyn, and through TikTok Go. It comes paired with the brand’s Signature Black Sesame Chili Oil, just how Keith likes it. Next up for the product: the freezer aisle and launching across the brand’s Canada shop locations.
