Snoopy and the Peanuts gang are heading to Burger King this holiday season, bringing new menu items, collectible merchandise, and a dose of nostalgia to the fast-food chain. Beginning December 1, participating U.S. restaurants will introduce a limited-time Peanuts menu featuring new food items, holiday beanies, collectible toys, and packaging inspired by Snoopy’s iconic red doghouse. The collaboration is Burger King’s latest effort to create experiences that appeal to customers of all ages. The centerpiece is the Peanuts Pack, an adult meal served in a collectible Snoopy Doghouse Box. Customers can choose a Whopper with Cheese or 10-piece Chicken Nuggets with Woodstock Golden Ranch, a new creamy, tangy dipping sauce. The meal also includes Charlie Brown Loaded Potato Tots, filled with cheese, bacon bits, sour cream, chives, and potatoes, along with a new Snoopy Cookies & Creme Pie featuring a chocolate cookie crust, vanilla-flavored creme filling, holiday sprinkles, and chocolate cookie crumbles. A medium fountain drink and one of two collectible Snoopy beanies complete the bundle. The beanies come in brown and red versions, featuring Snoopy resting on his doghouse or wearing a Santa hat. Burger King is also introducing a Peanuts-inspired King Jr. Meal featuring a hamburger, cheeseburger, or four-piece Chicken Nuggets, along with a side and beverage. Each meal comes in a Snoopy Doghouse Box and includes one of eight collectible toys featuring characters such as Charlie Brown, Lucy, Linus, Sally, and Snoopy. One option features Snoopy’s doghouse with stickers that children can use to decorate it. The promotion follows Burger King’s entertainment partnerships involving SpongeBob SquarePants, The Mandalorian, and Dragon Ball, but this collaboration has a more deliberate holiday connection. CMO Joel Yashinsky said the chain evaluates potential partnerships through consumer research. Burger King considered approximately 10 holiday collaborations before selecting Peanuts, whose decades-long association with Christmas made it a natural fit. The company worked with the Peanuts team over the past year to develop the promotion, seeking a property that could connect with children, parents, and grandparents. “What types of partnerships will connect with everyone from five to 95? We really try to find that multi-generational interest,” Yashinsky says. The promotion also supports Burger King’s efforts to rebuild its family business after years of marketing around its King mascot, whose unconventional appearance alienated some parents. “We had a mascot that a lot of moms, in particular, found creepy,” Yashinsky says. He believes the company’s previous marketing direction contributed to a long-term decline in its family business, leaving younger generations without the same connection to Burger King that their parents had. “We lost a generation of kids and families, and so now we’re working to get them back as part of our overall elevation and telling the story because they didn’t go up with Burger King, the Gen Zs of today,” he says. Burger King has since focused on creating more welcoming experiences for families, including revisiting elements of its earlier BK Kids program and exploring ways to give children greater choice during restaurant visits. The blaze, which broke out at a cold-storage facility in Kruiningen on 10 November, destroyed approximately 300,000 mozzarella planks, weighing 26 tonnes, disrupting supplies to the chicken restaurant chain across the UK. articles.title: Durigan prevê impacto inicial da reforma tributária sobre inflação
articles.titleKo: Durigan prevê impacto inicial da reforma tributária sobre inflação
articles.originalSummary: O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou, nesta terça-feira, 17, que a implementação da reforma tributária pode gerar pequeno impacto inicial sobre a inflação. A observação foi em resposta à preocupação manifestada por senadores com uma eventual alta do índice. Segundo o ministro, esse efeito tende a diminuir gradualmente à medida que as empresas se adaptem às novas regras tributárias e ajustem a formação de preços. “Pode haver algum pequeno impacto inflacionário, mas estamos passando por um processo em que os empresários vão aprender a precificar seus bens e serviços de acordo com a nova legislação tributária, considerando os créditos a que têm direito e os débitos pelos quais são responsáveis”, disse Durigan durante audiência na Comissão de Assuntos Econômicos (CAE) do Senado . Na avaliação do ministro, “à medida que essa precificação for sendo compreendida e ajustada ao longo dos próximos meses, teremos uma redução desse impacto inflacionário”. Ele acrescentou que o Ministério da Fazenda acompanhará o processo de perto. Tributação corporativa Durante a audiência, Durigan defendeu o avanço de uma reforma da tributação corporativa, incluindo a desoneração da folha de pagamentos. Segundo o ministro, a medida deve ser discutida diante das mudanças no mercado de trabalho e da crescente incorporação de tecnologia pelas empresas. “É importante desonerar a folha, mas sem causar um prejuízo significativo à Previdência”, afirmou. De acordo com Durigan, a discussão deve ocorrer com “total compromisso de neutralidade fiscal”, transferindo para outras bases de incidência tributária parte da carga atualmente cobrada sobre a folha de salários, como o faturamento ou o resultado das empresas. articles.title: Número de desempregados há dois anos ou mais é o menor já registrado
articles.titleKo: Número de desempregados há dois anos ou mais é o menor já registrado
articles.originalSummary: O número de desempregados que procuram emprego há pelo menos dois anos foi o menor em 14 anos no terceiro trimestre de 2026. O dado foi divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 18, pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ), na Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (Pnad) Contínua. O desemprego de longa duração atingia 971 mil pessoas entre julho e setembro deste ano, o menor contingente desde 2012, início da série histórica do IBGE. Essa foi a primeira vez que o grupo impactado pela desocupação de longo prazo somou menos de 1 milhão de pessoas. O número é resultado da redução de 17,6% do desemprego longo em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, quando havia 1,179 milhão de pessoas em busca de trabalho por mais de 24 meses. Também houve queda de 8% na comparação com o segundo trimestre de 2026, quando o desemprego longo já estava no menor patamar da série histórica, em 1,058 milhão. Mínimas históricas Os números do IBGE apontam que, no terceiro trimestre de 2026, o total de trabalhadores à procura de ocupação entre um e dois anos ficou em 590 mil, também o menor nível da série histórica. Ao se considerar o total de pessoas desempregadas há pelo menos um ano ─ isto é, somando também quem está à procura de ocupação há dois anos ou mais ─, o IBGE aponta 1,56 milhão de pessoas, também o menor número registrado desde 2012. A pesquisa mostra que o patamar mais alto de pessoas em busca de trabalho há pelo menos dois anos foi em 2021, no pico da pandemia de covid-19. Naquele ano, o contingente nessa condição se manteve acima de 3,5 milhões de pessoas, chegando a 3,810 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2021. No segundo trimestre de 2021, havia ainda 3 milhões de desempregados entre um e dois anos, e o total de desempregados há mais de um ano somava 6,74 milhões de trabalhadores. Mercado de trabalho aquecido De acordo com o analista da pesquisa, William Kratochwill, esse comportamento reflete um mercado de trabalho aquecido . “É um sinal de que o mercado está contratando cada vez mais”, diz. Ele detalha que, desde o fim da pandemia, as vagas vêm apresentando sinais de crescimento. “Se o mercado precisa da mão de obra, ele sempre pega primeiro aqueles que acha mais qualificados e, depois, vai trazendo as pessoas com tempo de busca maior para dentro da ocupação”, detalha. O levantamento do IBGE indica também que, no terceiro trimestre de 2026, havia 1,136 milhão de pessoas buscando trabalho há menos de um mês. Esse contingente teve um acréscimo de 0,8% na comparação com o mesmo trimestre de 2025 (eram 1,127 milhão). “Mostra uma maior rotação no mercado de trabalho”, sinaliza Kratochwill. Pnad Contínua A Pnad apura o comportamento no mercado de trabalho para pessoas com 14 anos ou mais e leva em conta todas as formas de ocupação, seja com ou sem carteira assinada, temporária ou por conta própria, por exemplo. Pelos critérios do instituto, só é considerada desocupada a pessoa que efetivamente procurou uma vaga 30 dias antes da pesquisa. São visitados 211 mil domicílios em todos os Estados e no Distrito Federal. O instituto já havia divulgado que o Brasil fechou o terceiro trimestre com desemprego em 5,2%, o menor para o período desde 2012. O país tinha 5,6 milhões de desempregados, patamar mínimo que perdia apenas para o último trimestre de 2025 (5,5 milhões). Do total de desocupados no trimestre até setembro, 17,2% estavam na busca por trabalho há pelo menos dois anos, enquanto 10,5% estavam na janela de um a dois anos. Cerca de metade (52,1%) estava no período de um mês a menos de um ano. Uma em cada cinco pessoas (20,2%) estava há menos de um mês nessa condição. Red Robin wants to focus on boosting its family and dinner business. Red Robin is finding its footing again, but the casual-dining chain sees an opportunity to turn its improving sales momentum into something more sustainable by giving customers new reasons to visit. After spending much of the past year rebuilding operations, introducing value offerings, and restructuring its finances, the burger chain is turning its attention to dinner, family dining, and menu innovation in 2027. The strategy follows a third quarter that delivered Red Robin’s strongest same-store sales performance in more than three years. Comps increased 3.9 percent, outperforming the industry by 70 basis points, according to Black Box Intelligence. Traffic declined 1.7 percent, but the company gained market share in areas where it competes with other restaurants. The company now wants to build on that success with new offerings targeting dinner and family occasions. “Going forward, you’ll see us put more focus on dinner and family occasion. This is a part of our business with room to grow and an area where our guests see a natural fit for Red Robin,” CEO David Pace said during the company’s Q3 earnings call. The chain is testing promotions and menu offerings aimed at families, with the results informing its plans for 2027. Its culinary pipeline includes potential additions across appetizers, salads, entrees, burgers, and beverages. Red Robin is also pursuing a barbell strategy that combines affordable meals with premium offerings. The company recently introduced its Prime Rib Stack Burger as a holiday special and expanded its Big Yummm platform with a $16.99 tier, giving customers opportunities to trade up. That strategy helped lift average check 5.6 percent during the third quarter, including a 3.4 percent increase from pricing and a 2.2 percent benefit from menu mix and discounts. The company also benefited from lapping the initial discounts associated with the Big Yummm launch. Despite the increase, Red Robin is exercising caution with additional pricing after previous increases affected its competitive positioning. The chain took one pricing action earlier this year and is evaluating its options for 2027. “As I look at ’27, I want to be equally cautious and try and figure out how can I get us positioned back to where I want to be within the competitive set of the industry, but still cover inflation, still make sure we’ve covered our cost structure and protected it,” Pace said. The company is also adjusting its marketing strategy under Scott Hudler, who joined as CMO in September, succeeding Russ Klein. Selling expenses increased to $9.4 million in the third quarter from $6.8 million a year earlier, driven by investments in the Big Yummm platform and personalized marketing. Pace expects spending in 2027 to be similar to or slightly below current levels, with more dollars directed toward consumer-facing advertising instead of internal marketing costs. Operational improvements are also contributing to Red Robin’s turnaround. Restaurant-level operating margin increased 90 basis points to 10.8 percent during the third quarter, including approximately 40 basis points of savings from labor efficiencies. The company is using AI to improve restaurant operations and eliminate redundant technology systems, along with supply chain initiatives aimed at reducing ingredient costs. articles.originalSummary: Os produtores brasileiros abateram 9,82 milhões de cabeças de bovinos sob algum tipo de serviço de inspeção sanitária no terceiro trimestre de 2026, uma queda de 13,4% em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025 , segundo os primeiros resultados das Pesquisas Trimestrais do Abate de Animais, do Leite, do Couro e da Produção de Ovos de Galinha, divulgados pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ). Na comparação com o segundo trimestre de 2026, houve redução de 8,4%. O volume resultou em uma produção de 2,62 milhões de toneladas de carcaças bovinas no terceiro trimestre de 2026, queda de 12,0% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. Ante o segundo trimestre, houve redução de 5,0%. Em sentido contrário, o abate de suínos somou 16,65 milhões de cabeças no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 5,2% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. Na comparação com o segundo trimestre deste ano, houve aumento de 6,1%. O peso acumulado das carcaças de suínos foi de 1,59 milhão de toneladas, crescimento de 6,4% na comparação anual e de 5,5% em relação ao segundo trimestre de 2026. O abate de frangos totalizou 1,79 bilhão de cabeças no terceiro trimestre, aumento de 5,8% ante igual período de 2025 e de 6,0% em relação ao segundo trimestre de 2026. O peso acumulado das carcaças de frango alcançou 3,86 milhões de toneladas, alta de 7,4% na comparação anual e de 3,3% em relação ao trimestre imediatamente anterior. China impõe tarifa à carne brasileira A carne bovina brasileira pagará uma tarifa total de 67% para entrar no mercado chinês. A cobrança adicional de 55% será aplicada sobre a tarifa regular de 12%, após o Brasil esgotar a cota anual de exportações estabelecida pelo país asiático. A medida preocupa frigoríficos e pecuaristas, que já avaliam antecipar abates e embarques para aproveitar a cota de 2027. O Brasil atingiu o limite de 1,106 milhão de toneladas previsto para 2026. Para o próximo ano, a cota sobe para 1,128 milhão de toneladas, mas representantes do setor estimam que o novo limite possa ser alcançado em março ou abril de 2027. O país asiático é o principal destino da carne bovina brasileira e ganhou espaço significativo nas exportações do setor na última década. De 2016 a 2025, o Brasil enviou 8,2 milhões de toneladas de carne bovina à China, movimentando US$ 42,3 bilhões. articles.title: Black Rock Gets Flexible as Development Costs Climb
articles.titleKo: Black Rock Gets Flexible as Development Costs Climb
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Black Rock Coffee Bar expects five California openings this year and 15 to 20 in 2027. Black Rock Coffee Bar’s next wave of growth is getting more expensive. But the chain sees an opportunity in buildings other brands leave behind. Average costs for its 2026 store class are coming in around $800,000 per location, accounting for tenant improvement allowances that offset the company’s investment. That compares with an initial expectation of $700,000 to $750,000 and approximately $650,000 last year. The increase hasn’t slowed Black Rock’s opening ambitions. The company raised its full-year target to 40 stores from 38 during its third-quarter earnings call and expects to substantially increase California development next year. Instead, it’s balancing different build types to manage capital and expand the pool of sites it can pursue. “We are actually balancing the capital in California with conversions, which are really helping,” CFO Rodd Booth said. READ MORE : Black Rock Finds More Room to Grow Beyond the Morning Rush Second-generation buildings with existing drive-thrus are a particular opportunity. They allow Black Rock to preserve a feature it considers central to the brand—its lobby—without taking on the same capital requirements as other development approaches in a higher-cost market. Booth said conversions are part of the strategy across Black Rock’s markets, not just California. But their value becomes especially apparent as the company builds its presence there. Black Rock expects five California openings this year and 15 to 20 in 2027. “It allows us to prioritize the lobby, but also not go out and really see the capital grow substantially in terms of a per-unit cost in California,” Booth said. That lobby also influences which properties Black Rock can make work. Asked what makes a good conversion, CEO Mark Davis pointed to a difference between Black Rock and competitors built exclusively around drive-thru service. Having a dining room means the chain doesn’t need the same long vehicle stack as a concept without one, he said. That gives Black Rock another option when evaluating existing buildings, alongside its ability to adapt to different site configurations. As other concepts close, Davis said, the development team is moving quickly to assess the spaces they leave behind. “We’re able to make a variety of different sites work,” he said. For landlords, the appeal extends beyond filling a vacancy. Davis said Black Rock’s flexibility and speed can help get properties through permitting, construction, and into operation sooner. “When you think of yourself as a landlord, they want somebody that can come in, that can go through the permitting quickly, that can adapt and get that open and get it going,” Davis said. “And what that does for them is it allows them to charge rent faster.” Becoming publicly traded last year has also helped generate interest from property owners, Davis added. Moving quickly, however, still requires work before a lease is signed. Davis said Black Rock has improved its pre-lease follow-up to better manage conversion costs. He connected that diligence to cash-on-cash returns of 35 percent in the first year and 40 percent in the second. Conversions are one part of the development mix. Black Rock also expects a near-term shift toward more reverse build-to-suit projects, which Booth said give the company greater control over planning and delivery. The benefit there is predictability. Booth said opening cadence has improved each quarter, with reverse build-to-suit stores helping Black Rock gain more control over when locations come online. The company opened 11 stores in Q3 across California, Arizona, Colorado, and Texas, finishing the period with 211. It has opened 35 for the year, with the remaining five expected in the coming weeks. Changes to the statutory tipping law, which include the new requirement for employers to hold formal consultations whenever a new tipping policy is introduced, are scheduled to take effect on 1 January. However, the draft revised code of practice on the fair and transparent distribution of tips, published this week, confirms that operators do not need to apply the new code until the next review of their tipping policy after 1 January 2027, which must be no later than three years from the date their current policy commenced. Peter Davies, client services partner at WMT Troncmaster Services, has welcomed the announcement of a transitional implementation period, saying it will help support operators and ensure they’re not distracted over the busy festive season.

articles.title: The Most Important Part of Modernizing a Landmark Hotel’s Menu is Learning What Not to Change
articles.titleKo: The Most Important Part of Modernizing a Landmark Hotel’s Menu is Learning What Not to Change
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Landmark hotel dining should not operate like a museum. Modernizing a dining program is often described in terms of what needs to change, whether that be new menus, new ingredients, new techniques, new presentations, or new ways of engaging today’s guest. Working as an executive chef at the landmark Biltmore Hotel has taught me that there is another, equally important question to ask: What shouldn’t we change? At a property with a century of stories embedded in its walls, dining traditions are not simply items on a menu. They become part of the hotel’s identity. Guests return not only for the cuisine, but for how an experience makes them feel – and often that feeling is tied to something they have enjoyed for years or hope to share with the next generation, which creates a different responsibility for a chef. Rather than working with a blank canvas, we are stewards of something that existed before us, while also being responsible for making it relevant to the guest sitting in front of us today. The challenge is knowing the difference between something that needs updating, and something that is timeless . Protect the Ritual, Evolve the Details The Biltmore’s Traditional Afternoon Tea is a perfect example. It’s truly a ritual and is about much more than tea and pastries. There is a certain anticipation that begins before the first cup is poured: the setting, the service, the tiers of savory and sweet offerings, the pacing and, most importantly, the invitation to slow down. At a time when so much of the modern dining experience has become faster, more casual and increasingly driven by convenience, there is something contemporary about asking guests to sit, linger and be present. That is why I believe some traditions should not be modernized simply for the sake of modernization. The menu can evolve with the seasons, ingredients can be refined, presentation can be updated, and techniques can become more sophisticated. However, the essence of the experience – the ritual, the sense of occasion, the gracious pace – deserves to remain, because we do not preserve a tradition by freezing it in time, but by understanding what makes it worth returning to. Start With Who You’re Feeding That same philosophy helps clarify where change is necessary, and Fairways, our classic golf club restaurant and bar, presents a very different opportunity. Its location connects it naturally to the golf course, but today’s leisure traveler does not define a resort dining experience only by the activity happening outside. One guest might have just finished 18 holes, while another spent the morning at the pool. A family may simply be looking for a relaxed lunch or dinner in a beautiful setting. A local guest may know the course intimately, while someone else has never picked up a club. The restaurant needs to welcome all of them. For Fairways, modernization means looking beyond the traditional definition of a golf restaurant and creating an experience that feels connected to its surroundings without being limited by them. The food should be approachable but thoughtfully prepared, the beverage program engaging, and the atmosphere inviting enough that guests want to stay awhile. The menu should also reflect how people dine while traveling today – whether casually, socially, after an activity, or simply because they have found a place they enjoy. In other words, the question isn’t, “What should we put on the menu?” The better question is, “Who are we feeding, and what do we want them to experience when they sit down?” Use Heritage as a Guide, Not a Constraint That distinction is particularly important in a landmark hotel, where heritage should inform the dining experience without becoming a constraint that keeps it from evolving. articles.title: Why 30-Day Labor Certification Option Should Matter to Restaurant Operators
articles.titleKo: Why 30-Day Labor Certification Option Should Matter to Restaurant Operators
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The immigration system is much more than a policy issue for operators today, it’s become a workforce issue that deserves a deeper look. Restaurants are acutely aware of the chronic shortage of workers that’s been plaguing numerous industries for years now. Both quick and full-service operators deal with the implications of this labor gap every single day, scrambling schedules, spiking overtime, and forcing managers onto the line. In recent years, that day-to-day pressure has gotten worse as the industry deals with higher expenses associated with labor, food supplies, and other costs, leaving even less room to absorb persistent vacancies and staffing disruptions. That means, more so than in previous years, unfilled positions like cooks, dishwashers and managers can have an outsized effect on operating hours, service levels, and profitability. Foreign-born workers already make up a critical component of the restaurant workforce, accounting for nearly one in four employees nationwide . Their role in the kitchen is even more pronounced, accounting for 44 percent of chefs and 33 percent of cooks. The immigration system is much more than a policy issue for operators today, it’s become a workforce issue that deserves a deeper look. As restaurants look for lawful, long-term solutions to the shortage of workers, delays in the employer-sponsored green card process can have serious operational consequences. One of those lawful pathways is the EB-3 visa program, which allows U.S. employers to sponsor foreign workers for permanent, full-time, year-round positions when they cannot find enough qualified and available U.S. workers to fill those jobs. For most employers using the EB-3 process, one of the first major steps is PERM, which is now taking around 10 months to complete. What PERM Actually Does PERM stands for Program Electronic Review Management and is the Department of Labor (DOL) labor-certification process used by employers pursuing permanent employment-based immigration. It is used to determine whether an employer has demonstrated that there are not sufficient able, willing, qualified and available U.S. workers for a permanent position. PERM exists to protect U.S. workers. Before a restaurant can sponsor a foreign worker for a permanent position, it must first test and prove the domestic labor market through required recruitment. The DOL must also be satisfied that employing the foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages or working conditions of similarly employed U.S. workers. In other words, PERM is not a way around local recruiting. Local recruiting is built into it. The Waiting Happens Early The biggest problem with PERM, as it stands today, is the wait time. As of October 31, 2026, DOL reported PERM applications at the analyst review stage were averaging 315 days over the 90-day period prior to the reporting date. For restaurant operators, that can include multiple hiring cycles. In that time, an eatery can lose employees, train replacements and still find itself recruiting yet again while one long-term labor certification is still being reviewed. In fact, that cycle can play out repeatedly during the wait. That matters because this staffing problem is no longer limited to one rough week here or there. It’s systemic and ongoing. While the entry-level labor pipeline shrinks, the pool of younger workers restaurants traditionally relied on is becoming less dependable. PERM would not solve turnover. It can matter, however, for operators struggling to keep permanent full-time jobs filled solely through domestic recruiting. articles.title: HTeaO Announces Record-Breaking Year for October Round-Up Campaign

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . HTeaO, the nation’s leading iced tea franchise, announced a record-breaking year for its annual October Round-Up campaign, raising $159,823.97 to benefit the Ryan Palmer Foundation Breast Cancer Initiative. Now in its sixth year, the campaign surpassed its previous fundraising record of $150,110 set in 2025, reflecting the continued generosity of HTeaO customers, franchise owners, and team members nationwide. From October 1–31, guests at all HTeaO locations nationwide were invited to round up their purchases to the nearest dollar, with 100% of donations funding the RPF Breast Cancer Initiative. The Initiative supports women at every stage, from early detection to treatment. Its programs include mobile mammograms, HOPE Kits for comfort, and cold cap therapy to help minimize hair loss. “Brewing Purpose is about more than giving back. It’s about bringing people together to make a difference in the communities we serve,” said Brittany Knollmiller, Director of Marketing of HTeaO. “Every October, we see that mission come to life as our guests, franchise partners, and team members rally behind a cause that touches so many families. This year’s record-breaking campaign is a reflection of that generosity and the impact we can make when everyone comes together, one small contribution at a time.” “When we started this partnership with HTeaO five years ago, Jen and I never imagined it would grow into what it is today. Setting a new record this year means a lot to our family and the Foundation. These funds will bring mobile mammograms to underserved communities and HOPE Kits into the hands of women going through treatment, and that’s what this is all about. To everyone who rounded up this October, and to the entire HTeaO family, thank you. We’re so grateful for your continued support of our Breast Cancer Initiatives.” The Ryan Palmer Foundation was established in 2003 by professional golfer and Amarillo native Ryan Palmer to provide opportunities for youth and support families in need. Inspired by his wife’s experience with chemotherapy, Palmer launched the Breast Cancer Initiative in 2019. Since then, the initiative has expanded access to early detection in underserved communities, and supported hundreds of breast cancer patients through the distribution of Hope Kits and Warrior Caps across the country. HTeaO celebrated the month-long campaign with pink straws at all locations in recognition of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a visible reminder of the brand’s ongoing commitment to community impact. With more than 180 locations nationwide, HTeaO continues to demonstrate its dedication to giving back through initiatives like the annual Round-Up campaign. By uniting franchise owners, team members, and customers under its Brewing Purpose platform, HTeaO aims to create positive change one cup at a time. articles.title: Shoppings projetam alta de 3% nas vendas na temporada de descontos
articles.titleKo: Shoppings projetam alta de 3% nas vendas na temporada de descontos
articles.originalSummary: Os shopping centers brasileiros estão otimistas para a Black Friday deste ano: 79% dos empreendimentos esperam crescimento no faturamento, com projeção de alta de 3% nas vendas em comparação com a edição de 2025, segundo levantamento da Associação Brasileira de Shopping Centers ( Abrasce ). O estudo aponta ainda que 71% projetam aumento nas vendas em relação ao ano anterior. Com descontos médios previstos de 37%, que podem chegar a 70%, a data, marcada para 27 de novembro, mobiliza os empreendimentos. O fluxo de visitantes deve crescer 1,7%, com 65% dos respondentes esperando movimento superior ao registrado em 2025. Já o ticket médio estimado é de R$ 237,35, acima do registrado no ano passado. “A Black Friday tem um papel estratégico para o varejo. Nos shoppings, a combinação de ofertas com a possibilidade de comparar produtos, contar com atendimento presencial e levar a compra na hora amplia a conveniência para o consumidor”, afirma Gabriella Oliveira, diretora de Planejamento Estratégico e Operações da Abrasce. Perfumaria lidera apostas de vendas na Black Friday Os descontos previstos pelos shoppings variam de 10% a 70%, com média de 37%. Perfumaria e cosméticos lideram as categorias com maior expectativa de destaque nas vendas, citadas por 74% dos respondentes. Na sequência aparecem eletrônicos e informática (65%), vestuário (63%), calçados (60%) e eletrodomésticos e eletroportáteis (57%). A liderança de perfumaria e cosméticos reforça o avanço da categoria na Black Friday. Em 2023, o segmento ocupava a sexta posição entre as apostas dos empreendimentos, citado por 43% dos participantes. Em 2024, passou ao segundo lugar, com 69%, e assumiu a liderança em 2025, com 73%. Shoppings diversificam ações promocionais Embora a Black Friday ocorra na última sexta-feira de novembro, as campanhas dos shoppings se distribuem por diferentes períodos. Neste ano, 42% dos empreendimentos concentrarão as ações entre sexta-feira e domingo, de 27 a 29 de novembro, enquanto 29% promoverão iniciativas durante toda a semana, de 23 a 29. Outros 11% estenderão as campanhas ao longo de novembro, e a mesma parcela concentrará as ações apenas na sexta-feira. As redes sociais são o principal canal de divulgação, citadas por 80% dos participantes. Entre as iniciativas para atrair consumidores, também estão roletas de prêmios (33%) e distribuição de brindes (27%). Além disso, 35% dos shoppings preveem ações especiais para a data, como a ampliação do horário de funcionamento até as 23h, para que os consumidores tenham mais tempo para aproveitar as promoções. articles.title: Estados Unidos entram em alerta após sucessivas panes tecnológicas
articles.titleKo: Estados Unidos entram em alerta após sucessivas panes tecnológicas
articles.originalSummary: Os Estados Unidos (EUA) entraram em alerta após as sucessivas panes tecnológicas que afetaram serviços críticos do país, desde a aviação civil, passando pelo sistema bancário, até mesmo o sistema de comunicação da Agência Nacional de Segurança (NSA), o órgão responsável pela inteligência do país. Ainda na semana passada, os serviços de comunicação da Microsoft saíram do ar, o que prejudicou serviços também no Brasil. Na última sexta-feira, 13, uma pane nos sistemas de controle da Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA) levou ao cancelamento de todos os voos nos EUA. Casos de panes tecnológicas continuaram ocorrendo nos dias seguintes. Na segunda-feira (16), o banco JPMorgan Chase registrou instabilidade em seus sistemas, prejudicando o acesso dos clientes a algumas ferramentas digitais. No mesmo dia, uma pane nos sistemas da empresa de transporte aéreo United Airlines levou a uma série de atrasos nos voos. Uma “falha generalizada” no sistema teria provocado o problema. Na terça-feira, 16, foi a vez da NSA relatar que sofreu uma “degradação temporária” durante uma manutenção de rotina, o que não teria prejudicado as “capacidades essenciais” da agência de inteligência do país, segundo reportou a CNN. Na quarta-feira, 17,novas panes tecnológicas foram registradas. Os sistemas da Apple, a fabricante de celulares e outros aparelhos móveis, ficaram fora do ar por algumas horas. Outro caso foi o da corretora de investimentos Charles Schwab, que concentra ativos de clientes de US$ 13 trilhões. A Schwab ficou fora do ar por algumas horas nessa terça-feira, 17, em pleno horário de funcionamento do mercado. Tanto as empresas , quanto o governo de Donald Trump, afirmam que as panes nos sistemas informáticos foram provocados por problemas técnicos, desde a instalação de roteadores no caso da FAA, quanto a atualização de sistemas por Inteligência Artificial (IA) que teriam provocado quedas de plataformas. O diretor de Inteligência Nacional dos EUA, Jay Clayton, afirmou à imprensa que não há indícios de que as panes tenham sido provocadas por ataques cibernéticos de atores mal intencionados. “Não vemos indícios de um ataque cibernético coordenado. E também não vemos indícios de atividade patrocinada por um Estado”, disse Clayton à Fox Business. O presidente Trump minimizou os episódios, dizendo que tudo estaria “bem”. Ele culpou a administração democrata de Joe Biden por não modernizar o sistema da FAA, que teria causado a paralisação completa do setor aéreo dos EUA. O secretário de Estado Marco Rubio afastou a hipótese de ataques hackers coordenados ou interferência de Estados estrangeiros, como o Irã, ainda em guerra com os EUA. Rubio reconheceu que os acontecimentos são “perturbadores”, mas destacou que não há evidência de que tenham sido causados por ataques cibernéticos. “Não estamos sofrendo um ataque sistêmico”, disse a repórteres. O pesquisador do Núcleo de Estudos Estratégicos em Comunicação, Cognição e Computação, Reynaldo Aragon, avaliou à Agência Brasil que ainda não é possível saber se houve ataques cibernéticos em alguns casos, mas aponta que essas panes expõem certa fragilidade dos EUA. “O maior país do ocidente e do mundo em economia e tecnologia ficou quatro horas e meia com os voos todos cancelados. Ou seja, o Estado americano perdeu o controle do seu próprio espaço aéreo durante esse período. Isso é muito grave do ponto de vista histórico”, disse. Congressistas questionam Congressistas norte-americanos têm considerado as respostas das autoridades ligadas à Casa Branca como insuficientes. Mesmo aliados do presidente Donald Trump têm levantado suspeitas sobre as razões das panes e pedido mais informações. O senador republicano do Missouri, Josh Hawley, disse a jornalistas que se “tudo isso for uma coincidência, é a maior coincidência da história do mundo”. “Todas essas interrupções, talvez seja porque alguém desconectou um roteador no Arkansas, ou algo assim. Não sei, francamente, acho isso um pouco difícil de acreditar. Port

articles.title: Black Friday 2026: fatia de consumidores decididos a comprar salta para 32,3%
articles.titleKo: Black Friday 2026: fatia de consumidores decididos a comprar salta para 32,3%
articles.originalSummary: A aproximação da Black Friday 2026 acelerou as decisões de consumo no País. Uma pesquisa do Reclame Aqui aponta que a fatia de consumidores decididos a comprar na data saltou de 19% em agosto para 32,3% em novembro, um avanço de 13,3 pontos percentuais. O movimento é acompanhado pela redução da indecisão, que recuou 9,4 pontos percentuais, de 61% para 51,6%, e da rejeição ao evento. Apenas 16,1% dos entrevistados afirmaram que pretendem ficar de fora. Há também potencial de renovação do público, já que 54,2% dos consumidores dispostos a comprar ou ainda indecisos são estreantes no evento ou voltam a participar após ficarem de fora da edição de 2025. Compras se espalham por novembro A distribuição do orçamento indica que a tradicional sexta-feira de promoções perdeu exclusividade. Em vez de concentrar os gastos em um único dia, quase metade dos consumidores (48,1%) decidiu não definir um orçamento com antecedência e pretende acompanhar as ofertas ao longo de novembro. Apenas 17,4% dos entrevistados planejam concentrar a maior parte das compras na data oficial da Black Friday, enquanto os demais preferem aproveitar promoções antecipadas ou decidir no momento da compra. Orçamento limita compras na Black Friday O levantamento identificou uma mudança na percepção dos consumidores que decidiram não comprar nesta edição. A desconfiança em relação às promoções, associada à ideia de que o evento não oferece descontos reais, prática conhecida como “metade do dobro”, deixou de ser o principal motivo para não comprar. O percentual recuou de 51,6% em agosto para 15,6% em novembro. Atualmente, os principais obstáculos ao consumo são de ordem financeira: 34,9% dos que pretendem ficar de fora afirmam que o orçamento não permite gastos extras; 34,5% dizem não precisar de nenhum produto no momento. IA auxilia pesquisa O consumidor também passou a enxergar a Inteligência Artificial não apenas como novidade ou curiosidade, mas como uma ferramenta prática de apoio às compras e de controle do orçamento. Para a Black Friday, o uso da tecnologia se concentra em atividades de pesquisa e economia: 66,3% utilizam a IA para pesquisar as características dos produtos desejados; 40,2% recorrem à ferramenta para comparar preços e encontrar ofertas; 25,8% usam a tecnologia para localizar lojas que vendem os itens procurados. Reputação pesa na decisão de compra A reputação das empresas também deve influenciar as decisões de compra na Black Friday 2026. Segundo a pesquisa, 76,1% dos entrevistados afirmam que pretendem consultar o Reclame Aqui durante o evento. A preocupação vai além dos descontos oferecidos: Reputação das lojas: 69,1% pesquisam o histórico das empresas para verificar se cumprem prazos e entregam os produtos anunciados; Suporte pós-venda: 34,1% analisam o histórico de reclamações e o índice de resposta das marcas para evitar problemas com trocas, devoluções e assistência técnica; Segurança digital: 20,9% utilizam ferramentas de verificação para verificar a legitimidade das páginas antes de inserir dados de pagamento. articles.title: CCJ aprova punição a fraude financeira para evitar ‘caso Americanas’
articles.titleKo: CCJ aprova punição a fraude financeira para evitar ‘caso Americanas’
articles.originalSummary: A Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) do Senado aprovou, nesta quarta-feira, 18, por 15 a 0, o Projeto de Lei 2.091/2023 , que cria um tipo penal para punir fraudes contábeis no mercado de capitais. Um dos objetivos é evitar casos semelhantes ao das Lojas Americanas. O texto ainda precisará passar por uma votação suplementar antes de ir para a Câmara. Durante a tramitação, o texto foi alterado pelo relator, Oriovisto Guimarães (PSDB-PR), que retirou quatro dos cinco novos crimes previstos na proposta original e manteve a tipificação da fraude contábil. Pela versão atual, cometerá crime quem fraudar a contabilidade ou fornecer documentos falsos à auditoria independente, inserindo operações inexistentes, dados inexatos ou deixando de incluir operações efetivamente realizadas. A pena prevista é de reclusão de dois a seis anos, além de multa. O texto também estabelece o aumento das penas de metade até o dobro, a depender da magnitude dos prejuízos, da vantagem ilícita obtida, do abalo à confiança no sistema financeiro nacional ou da pluralidade de vítimas. Em caso de reincidência, a pena poderá chegar ao triplo. Outro trecho prevê a possibilidade de o condenado ficar inabilitado para exercer atividade empresarial, impedido de ocupar cargos em conselhos de administração e fiscais, diretorias ou gerências, além de não poder gerir empresas por mandato ou gestão de negócio. Esse impedimento poderá durar por até cinco anos após o trânsito em julgado. O texto também altera a Lei dos Crimes contra o Sistema Financeiro Nacional para aperfeiçoar o crime de induzir ou manter em erro sócios, acionistas, investidores ou repartições públicas sobre a situação financeira, contábil ou patrimonial de uma sociedade, por meio da omissão ou prestação de informações falsas. A pena passa a ser de reclusão de dois a seis anos e multa. Na proposta original, a autora, senadora Augusta Brito (PT-CE), estabelecia cinco novos crimes: indução a erro no mercado de capitais, fraude contábil, influência imprópria em auditorias, falsidade ideológica em manifestação e administração infiel. O projeto também estabelecia o dever de agir de diretores, gerentes, administradores, executivos, conselheiros, auditores independentes, consultores e analistas para evitar os crimes. O relator considerou que parte das tipificações era excessivamente abrangente ou repetia crimes já previstos na legislação. O caso das Lojas Americanas veio à tona em janeiro de 2023, quando a companhia revelou inconsistências contábeis estimadas inicialmente em R$ 20 bilhões, relacionadas principalmente à contabilização de operações de risco sacado como despesas com fornecedores, em vez de dívidas bancárias. A prática teria inflado artificialmente os resultados da empresa e ocultado seu real endividamento, levando à descoberta de um rombo bilionário, à crise financeira da varejista e ao pedido de recuperação judicial. O episódio provocou prejuízos a investidores e credores e levantou questionamentos sobre a atuação de administradores e auditorias independentes. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Naomi Matsui). Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop, announced today the opening of a new shop at EastVillage on November 14, the 425-acre mixed-use development taking shape along East Parmer Lane in Northeast Austin’s Tech Ridge corridor. Serving EastVillage residents, nearby neighborhoods and employees throughout one of Austin’s largest technology and employment centers, the new Potbelly brings the brand’s signature neighborhood experience to the community. It joins more than 60 shops operating throughout Texas and offers the toasty warm sandwiches the brand is known for, alongside wraps, signature salads, hand-dipped shakes, freshly baked cookies and other craveable menu items. “EastVillage is creating something Northeast Austin has needed – a place where residents, employees and visitors can spend time together without having to head across the city,” said Jignesh Patel, who is opening his third Potbelly with business partner Nitin Patel, as part of a 15-unit Central Texas development agreement. “This is a natural home for Potbelly. We’re excited to serve the people who already live and work nearby while growing alongside a community that is just beginning to take shape.” Designed to bring a more walkable, downtown-style experience to a traditionally car-oriented part of the city, EastVillage is adding restaurants like Potbelly, along with retail, entertainment, residences, office space and outdoor recreation. Its plans include a 1.5-acre village green, more than five miles of hike-and-bike trails and a 150-acre natural preserve. Following recent shop openings in Georgetown and Hutto, Jignesh and Nitin were drawn to the energy surrounding EastVillage and the opportunity to serve a unique mix of guests. To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a celebration on December 14. Guests can also enjoy a ribbon-cutting, a spin wheel activation and a Potbelly Perks Plinko game for chances to win exclusive merchandise, free food and other prizes. The new shop will offer convenient options for lunch, dinner and everything in between. Regular operating hours are 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Delivery, order ahead and catering are available in-shop, through Potbelly.com and in the Potbelly App, with third-party delivery services also available. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where members can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. To sign up, visit www.potbelly.com/perks. For more information about the new Potbelly location, visit www.potbelly.com. The post Potbelly Opens in Northeast Austin appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Whether through custom designed holiday cards mailed to your community or seasonal flyers handed out at pop up markets or festivals to spread the word, customers pay attention to the details, especially when they make a spot standout during the hectic holiday rush. The refreshed core menu and holiday offerings are now available at Ruby Tuesday locations nationwide. For more information or to find a location near you, visit www.rubytuesday.com. Brodeur also inherited a team that understood the restaurant. She did not replace any employees, which created continuity during a major personal transition. Also, her daughter was born near the time Brodeur became the franchisee. The circumstances forced her to balance motherhood with first-time ownership. Brodeur could not immediately spend as much time inside the shop as she envisioned, so she relied on employees to run shifts as she handled administrative work. She recalls making business calls from her hospital bed the day after giving birth. Six days later, her daughter joined her for a photo shoot at the restaurant. “I had to make things work, and it’s something that I’m proud of saying that I was able to do this at that time, and I wouldn’t have changed it for anything,” she says. She needed to monitor food costs, labor, and other expenses that had not fallen within her employee duties. “I definitely think it would have to be on the financial side of things, making sure that all of my costs are where they should be, and all of my labor is where it should be,” says Brodeur, discussing what surprised her the most about franchise ownership. The 2027 report findings point to a generation reshaping when, why and what people eat. Yum! Brands, Inc. today released its second annual Food Trends Report, “What’s Next in Dining,” developed with its in-house marketing strategy, consumer insights and innovation agency Collider Lab. With more than 44,000 restaurants across its KFC, Taco Bell and Habit Burger & Grill brands, Yum! draws on global consumer insights, cultural analysis and menu testing to explore how all-day snacking, more memorable restaurant experiences and globally inspired flavors are changing what people crave and where they dine. The 2027 report findings point to a generation reshaping when, why and what people eat. Among the biggest takeaways: Gen Z is officially in permanent snack mode: 20% of restaurant visits among QSR customers ages 18–24 are for snack occasions, double the rate of customers 25 and older. Restaurants are becoming destinations: Younger consumers are nearly twice as likely to choose a restaurant that offers a more special experience. Global flavors are bringing a new sense of adventure to familiar favorites: Globally inspired menu ideas accounted for 35% of the top concepts ranked highest on modernity in the U.S., up from just 5% in 2025. “The next generation isn’t organizing its day around three meals, and it isn’t choosing restaurants on convenience alone,” said Ken Muench, Chief Marketing Officer, Yum! Brands and Co-Founder of Collider Lab. “People want food that fits the moment, an experience that feels worth having and a chance to discover something new. Understanding those shifts is central to our Raise the B.A.R. priorities and our work to Battle for the Future Consumer. This research helps us look beyond what’s popular today to what our brands can do to earn the next visit.” The 2027 Food Trends Building on these findings, Yum! identified three trends shaping how consumers eat, what they crave and the experiences they seek. A snapshot of the findings is below, an animated infographic is on Yum.com, and you can download the full report here . Perma Snack Mode The next generation isn’t waiting for breakfast, lunch or dinner. Snacking, sipping and grazing throughout the day are becoming a way of life, with smaller portions, sweets and drinks increasingly part of everyday QSR occasions. The Snack Generation: Among QSR customers ages 18–24, 20% of restaurant visits are for snack occasions, compared with 10% among customers 25 and older. They also visit 1.2x as often from 2–4 p.m. and twice as often from 8–10 p.m. Sips Have Staying Power: QSR customers ages 18–24 are 1.3x more likely to order a beverage than customers 25 and older, as specialty drinks like KFC’s KWENCH lineup become an occasion in their own right. Small Bites, Big Cravings: Across more than 600 menu ideas tested by Yum! Brands, sweets accounted for half of the top 10 all-time performers. The Crave for Experience While ease, speed and convenience remain important, consumers are placing greater value on how a QSR experience makes them feel. Being seen as “very cool” is now the No. 1 attribute driving momentum in QSR, with elevated details across people, product and place shaping the overall experience. Hospitality Makes the Difference: Employee hospitality remains the top driver of guest experience, putting a premium on personal touches like Taco Bell’s Live Más Café “Bellristas,” who bring a more welcoming, personalized approach to service. Packaging That Performs: In menu testing, ideas with elevated packaging, like Habit Burger & Grill’s specially designed family meal box featuring burgers, fries and dipping sauces, scored an average of four percentage points higher across incrementality, uniqueness and buzz. The Christmas Vacation Feast is stacked with festive favorites. Jimmy John’s is bringing a little Griswold-style chaos to the holidays with the Christmas Vacation Feast, a limited-time meal inspired by the legendary holiday film, National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation . Packed with festive flavors, collectible swag and plenty of over-the-top holiday spirit, it’s everything fans love about the movie, served Jimmy John’s style. The Christmas Vacation Feast is stacked with festive favorites, including the Jelly of the Month Club Sandwich, Stuffing Flavored Jimmy Chips and the Griswold Family Chaos Cookie, complete with a Crunch Enhancer Clark Griswold himself would appreciate. Everything comes wrapped in custom National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation-inspired packaging, bringing a little extra holiday chaos to every order. Stuffing Flavored Jimmy Chips deliver all the savory, herby goodness of classic holiday stuffing in a kettle-cooked chip. All the stuffing flavor, none of the prep work. The Griswold Family Chaos Cookie does what the Griswolds would do: goes completely overboard with chocolate chips, festive candies, peppermint, pretzels, marshmallows, sprinkles and a cornflake “Crunch Enhancer” inspired by Clark’s unforgettable holiday creation. The Cousin Eddie-inspired turtleneck dickie comes in four festive colors. Featuring fan-favorite movie quotes like “You Serious, Clark?” and “Save the Neck,” the collectible dickies offer four styles worthy of any holiday gathering. While the Jelly of the Month Club is sure to get gobbled up this holiday, those craving their go-to Jimmy John’s Favorite sandwich can customize the Christmas Vacation Feast with any Toasted sandwich, chips, or cookie. For fans collecting all four of the Cousin Eddie-inspired dickies, whether it’s for stocking stuffers or an ugly sweater party, each will also be available for individual purchase. “When it comes to the holidays, Clark Griswold set the bar impossibly high,” said Suzanne DeRouchie, Vice President of Integrated Marketing Communications at Jimmy John’s. “We wanted to capture that same over-the-top energy in a way only Jimmy John’s could. From festive new menu items to the Cousin Eddie-inspired dickie, the Christmas Vacation Feast gives fans a delicious excuse to lean into a little holiday chaos.” The holiday fun doesn’t stop at the menu. LaSalle Dr., the festive takeover tips its hat to both the film’s setting and Jimmy John’s roots near the site of its first restaurant. From a squirrel plushie and Clark-inspired hockey jersey to a Cousin Eddie-inspired trapper hat, the collection is packed with gifts no Jelly of the Month Club could ever top. articles.title: Vivara inaugura loja “ícone” no Shopping JK Iguatemi
articles.titleKo: Vivara inaugura loja “ícone” no Shopping JK Iguatemi
articles.originalSummary: A Vivara inaugurou uma nova loja no Shopping JK Iguatemi, em São Paulo, reforçando sua presença em um dos principais endereços de luxo da capital paulista. A empresa informou que o espaço representa um movimento de renovação da experiência de compra, com um projeto que preserva a identidade da joalheria brasileira enquanto soma uma interpretação contemporânea de seus elementos tradicionais. Com arquitetura assinada pelo Estúdio Tupi, o projeto parte do conceito de “de-novo”, uma proposta que revisita os elementos já reconhecidos no universo visual da Vivara para reorganizá-los em outras formas e composições. A ideia é construir uma nova identidade para o espaço mantendo a tradição da marca e estabelecendo um diálogo entre sua trajetória e uma nova maneira de apresentar suas joias. “Ao longo de sua história, a Vivara construiu uma identidade muito forte e acreditamos que evoluir também significa encontrar novas formas de expressar essa essência. A loja ícone no JK Iguatemi representa esse movimento, ao reunir a tradição da nossa joalheria a uma visão contemporânea de varejo. Queremos continuar proporcionando experiências que fortaleçam a relação dos nossos clientes com a marca”, afirmou Marina Kaufman, presidente do Conselho de Administração da Vivara . A proposta ganha forma por meio da combinação de materiais, texturas e volumes. Revestimentos em pedra, marcenaria em madeira, balcões de mármore rosado e um piso de desenho geométrico criam um ambiente que equilibra sofisticação e contemporaneidade. As vitrines, os expositores e as áreas de atendimento integram essa composição, com espaços pensados para valorizar as joias e proporcionar uma experiência de compra única, individual e acolhedora. Milk & Honey, the Southern-inspired flagship brand of Thompson Restaurants, a family-run hospitality company, officially opens its newest restaurant at Tysons Corner Center on Wednesday, Nov. 18. The brand’s 22nd location is also its largest and most elevated to date, and it introduces Milk & Honey Express, a fast-casual concept next door. The restaurant is located at 1961 Chain Bridge Road, G21U, in Tysons, inside one of the Washington region’s premier shopping, dining and entertainment destinations. It follows back-to-back openings in Gainesville and Manassas this summer and marks the brand’s latest push into Northern Virginia. “Opening Milk & Honey at Tysons Corner Center is a milestone for our brand,” said Alex Berentzen, chief operating officer of Thompson Restaurants. “As our largest location to date, it reflects the continued evolution of the concept and brings our signature hospitality and Southern-inspired cuisine to one of the most dynamic destinations in the DMV. We’re also proud to introduce Milk & Honey Express, a convenient new way for guests on the go to enjoy their favorites whether you’re shopping, working or visiting Tysons.” At approximately 4,907 square feet, the Tysons restaurant is the brand’s most ambitious project yet. An open kitchen lets guests see the energy and craftsmanship behind the culinary operation, and spacious dining areas are designed for everyday meals as well as larger social gatherings. The restaurant is visible and accessible directly from inside the mall. Next door, Milk & Honey Express serves signature breakfast items, coffee beverages, quick-service meals and select dinner offerings for shoppers, commuters and guests on the go, with online ordering through Thompson Restaurants’ website. Together, the two make up the first dual-concept experience in the brand’s history. The restaurant seats 230 guests across 156 indoor seats, a 10-seat bar and a 64-seat patio. The opening is expected to create more than 100 jobs across management, culinary, hospitality and service roles. Guests can enjoy the brand’s full menu of Southern-inspired favorites throughout the day, including signature dishes such as Smothered Chicken and Biscuits, Chicken and Biscoff Waffles, Fried Green Tomatoes, Crispy Salmon Hash, House-Rubbed Steak and Eggs, and Carolina Low Country Gumbo. The beverage program features signature cocktails including the Biscoff Espresso Martini, Jim Beam Blackberry Smash and Spicy Guava Margarita, alongside a selection of mocktails. articles.title: O que Jeff Bezos tem a ver com a escolha de Robert Pattinson como o novo James Bond?
articles.titleKo: O que Jeff Bezos tem a ver com a escolha de Robert Pattinson como o novo James Bond?
articles.originalSummary: O fundador da Amazon, Jeff Bezos, afirmou, na terça-feira, 17, que esteve “bastante envolvido” na escalação de Robert Pattinson como o próximo James Bond no 26º filme de 007, que terá direção de Denis Villeneuve. Segundo informações da Reuters , a declaração ocorreu na conferência Silicon Valley & The World, organizada pelo Semafor. A relação entre a Amazon e 007 veio a público em 2022, quando a multinacional de e-commerce finalizou a compra da MGM, estúdio-mãe da franquia de James Bond. Em fevereiro de 2025, as ligações se estreitaram ainda mais: a companhia assumiu o controle dos direitos criativos sobre o filme, que pertencia à família Broccoli desde 1962. Como declarou Bezos, a Amazon foi decisiva na escolha de Pattinson, conhecido por seus papéis em Crepúsculo e Batman, para encarnar o lendário espião. A empresa teria reduzido a lista de candidatos e realizado os testes de câmera com cinco atores – onde cada um interpretou três cenas com figurinos completos e em cenários de filmagem -, informou a Reuters . “Nos reunimos na sexta-feira para passar algumas horas assistindo a todos os testes de câmera e analisando tudo”, disse o empresário na conferência. Pattinson, de 40 anos, venceu uma disputa que contava com Nicholas Hoult (Superman), Josh O’Connor (Rivais), Callum Turner (Só Por Uma Noite) e Jack Lowden (Slow Horses). Bezos também revelou que, inicialmente, a escalação de Pattinson como James Bond lhe causava certo receio devido ao seu já consolidado alcance em Hollywood: “Pensamos que talvez devêssemos escolher alguém um pouco menos conhecido”. Nos testes de câmera, entretanto, ficou evidente que o ator seria o próximo James Bond, contou o presidente da Amazon. Robert Pattinson sucederá Daniel Craig como o protagonista da mais famosa franquia de espionagem. Experiente em sucessos de bilheteria, o ator já esteve em dois deles só neste ano: A Odisseia, de Christopher Nolan, que acaba de chegar ao streaming com 90 minutos de bastidores, e O Drama, de Kristoffer Borgli. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Maria Fernanda Barros). That capability fits the diverse communities Checkers & Rally’s serves and sets the deployment apart from single language systems. “At Checkers & Rally’s, speed, convenience and accuracy are central to the drive-thru experience,” said Dave Pelletier, Chief Operating Officer at Checkers & Rally’s. “Our partnership with Hi Auto reflects our continued investment in technology that supports restaurant operations while making the ordering experience more seamless for our guests. articles.title: Your Holiday Campaign is Ready. Your Franchisees Aren’t
articles.titleKo: Your Holiday Campaign is Ready. Your Franchisees Aren’t
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Every year, QSR marketing teams ship holiday campaigns they’re proud of. Then those campaigns hit 800 franchisees, each with their own stores, local priorities and ad buys across every conceivable channel. The store near the mall wants to push gift cards and grab-and-go. The suburban store wants family bundles. The franchisee two exits down the highway is fighting a new competitor and needs a sharper price. Not to mention the different state regulations that need to be catered for. They all want to utilize the national creative because they understand the value of the brand they’ve bought into,but none of them can use it exactly as it is. So they email corporate. Corporate adds their request or approvals to the queue, and by the time the localized version comes back, the week that mattered is gone. That’s the real holiday problem for franchise brands, and it lives in the last mile, when getting it wrong is the most expensive. National sets the tone. Local wins the sale. Nobody’s arguing against national campaigns. They build the brand, set the look and keep the message consistent across a thousand doors. That job matters. But customers don’t buy from a national campaign. They buy from a store, on a street, against whoever’s across the road. Demand, pricing and competition change from one neighborhood to the next, and over the holidays those gaps get wider. A location near a shopping center might see its busiest period during last-minute holiday shopping, while another may depend on catering orders or family meals. Both are working from the same national campaign, but their immediate priorities are different. Most franchise marketing systems still treat every restaurant as if it were the same. The answer isn’t to abandon the national playbook. It’s to build it so stores can adapt it without asking permission for every change. The bottleneck is process. QSR brands aren’t short on ideas. What they’re short on is time and budget. They can’t produce enough content quickly enough across every channel for every market. Think about what one holiday promo needs before it works locally: different prices, different offers, store hours and addresses, plus a dozen formats from window clings to Instagram stories. Every change can mean a request, a revision and an approval. Multiply that by a few hundred stores and your marketing team is now running a design agency without the resources to do it properly. And the requests don’t all arrive at once. One franchise needs a new offer approved on Monday, another needs updates creative for a location promotion on Wednesday. A third discovers that the available assets don’t fit the advertising channel they are using. Franchisees miss their moment. Corporate drowns in admin and still can’t see what’s running where. Making more content won’t fix that. Getting it through the system faster will. Where AI earns its keep. There’s plenty of noise about AI writing entire campaigns. For franchise brands, the bigger win is far less glamorous:eliminating the busywork. Resizing. Swapping prices. Updating store details. Reformatting for every channel. Chasing sign-off on routine changes that already meet brand requirements.A person doesn’t need to touch every one of those tasks. Lock the brand elements nationally, open up the fields franchisees can change, and let predefined rules handle the routine approvals. Location, offer and call to action stay editable. Logo, layout and tone stay locked. Corporate reviews the exceptions instead of every flyer. This also makes it easier to respond when plans change. If a promotion needs to be updated across multiple locations, approved changes can be made without restarting the creative process for every store. People still own the strategy, the brand standards and the big calls. Automation just stops them from spending December resizing banners. Freedom

articles.originalSummary: A Operação Cash Out, que atingiu um grupo empresarial do ramo das bets , identificou que a organização criminosa movimentou cerca de R$ 11 bilhões no exercício de 2025. O negócio, sediado em Curaçao, ocultava os recursos ilícitos por meio de operações de câmbio, utilização de apostadores fictícios e empresas laranjas. Segundo o secretário especial da Receita Federal, Robinson Barreirinhas, o Fisco identificou um padrão entre empresas de apostas que operavam irregularmente para acumular recursos e pagar a outorga de R$ 30 milhões, necessária para regularizar suas atividades. “Esse modus operandi perverso se refere a evasão de divisas, lavagem de dinheiro, ocultação da origem de recursos por meio de operações de câmbio, algumas delas com remessas, outras apenas simulando a remessa e utilização de apostadores laranjas”, destacou o secretário. “Esses recursos voltavam do exterior e nós estamos seguros que foram utilizados depois para o próprio pagamento da outorga regular. Nós estamos tratando aqui de uma casa de apostas que é bastante infiltrada no ecossistema do esporte no Brasil, patrocinando diversos clubes, programas de televisão, figuras que se aproximam de figuras da mídia nacional”, afirmou Barreirinhas. De acordo com o chefe do Fisco, a organização criminosa em questão utilizava com frequência empresas laranjas ligadas ao ramo de eventos para ocultar os recursos oriundos da exploração ilegal de bets. “Aquele benefício fiscal do Perse se prestava muito a esse tipo de lavagem de dinheiro, porque as empresas de eventos não pagavam nenhum tributo federal sobre essas receitas”, lembrou Barreirinhas. “Era o instrumento perfeito de lavagem de dinheiro”, acrescentou. articles.title: Novo SAC na véspera da Black Friday: o que o varejo precisa ajustar já
articles.titleKo: Novo SAC na véspera da Black Friday: o que o varejo precisa ajustar já
articles.originalSummary: Regra nova às vésperas da data mais movimentada do ano. Você provavelmente tem uma história de SAC para contar. A musiquinha que não termina, o menu que dá voltas e devolve você ao início, a terceira atendente que pede, com toda a educação do mundo, que você explique tudo de novo. Quem trabalha no varejo conhece essa cena dos dois lados do balcão. Desde 2 de novembro, boa parte dessas histórias deixou de ser só irritante e passou a ser descumprimento de norma. Nesse dia entrou em vigor o Decreto nº 13.135/2026, publicado no Diário Oficial em 13 de outubro. O texto revogou o Decreto nº 11.034/2022 e reescreveu as regras do Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor. O mercado continua chamando de “Lei do SAC”. Vou chamar assim também, embora tecnicamente seja um decreto, e esse detalhe tem consequências que comento mais adiante. O calendário não ajudou. Foram 20 dias entre a publicação e a vigência, sem regra de transição, para rever URA, chatbot, escala de atendentes e contrato com call center. E o primeiro grande teste já está marcado: a Black Friday, no dia 27. Afinal, isso vale para o varejo? Essa é a pergunta que mais tenho ouvido, e a resposta honesta é: depende do que a empresa vende e de como vende. O decreto continua mirando, em primeiro lugar, os serviços regulados pelo governo federal, como telefonia, energia, planos de saúde e aviação. A novidade é que agora entram expressamente os serviços financeiros, de pagamento e de crédito oferecidos por meios digitais sob supervisão do Banco Central. Para o varejo, isso não é detalhe. Carteira digital, cartão próprio, conta de pagamento e parcelamento via fintech parceira são, hoje, parte do negócio de muitas redes. Outra mudança: as agências e os órgãos reguladores de cada setor passam a definir os critérios de enquadramento. Ou seja, a fotografia completa de quem está dentro ainda vai se formar nos CDC (Código de Defesa do Consumidor) continua valendo inteiro, e eu não me surpreenderia se Procons e juízes passassem a usar os parâmetros do novo SAC como régua do que é um atendimento razoável. Quem estiver longe demais dela vai ter dificuldade para se explicar. O que muda na prática Gente de verdade, todos os dias. A regra antiga pedia atendimento humano por pelo menos 8 horas diárias. Agora ele é obrigatório das 8h às 20h, inclusive aos sábado, domingo e feriado, tanto no telefone quanto nos canais digitais. Além disso, pelo menos um canal eletrônico precisa funcionar 24 horas . Para quem dimensiona equipe, é aqui que a conta muda. O robô pode ficar, desde que abra a porta. O decreto não proíbe inteligência artificial nem chatbot. Eles podem fazer triagem e até resolver a demanda. A condição é que o consumidor consiga falar com uma pessoa em qualquer etapa, sem ter de informar CPF, número do pedido ou qualquer dado antes disso. Cinco níveis e acabou. Menus eletrônicos e URA não podem passar de cinco níveis. As opções de cancelar e de falar com um atendente têm de aparecer em todos eles, a começar pelo primeiro. Também fica proibido o velho “para isso, acesse nosso aplicativo”: o canal que recebeu a demanda resolve, salvo quando o atendimento presencial for mesmo indispensável. No telefone, quem pede para falar com uma pessoa deve ser atendido em até 20 segundos em pelo menos 80% dos casos, e em até 5 minutos nos demais, ressalvada regra setorial própria. O consumidor tem de ser informado do tempo estimado de espera. Se a ligação cair, a empresa tem 5 minutos para retornar, com o mesmo protocolo e sem começar do zero. Silêncio publicitário. O decreto anterior admitia propaganda na espera, desde que o consumidor consentisse. Isso acabou. Não pode haver publicidade em nenhuma etapa do atendimento, com ou sem consentimento. Em plena temporada de ofertas, convém ouvir de novo cada mensagem gravada. Outra mudança que o consumidor vai sentir logo: a empresa deve acompanhar a demanda até o fim e não pode exigir que o consumidor recomece. Pedir que ele repita o que já disse só é aceito qua

articles.title: Drive-Thru AI Is Freeing Up Crews. What Happens Next?
articles.titleKo: Drive-Thru AI Is Freeing Up Crews. What Happens Next?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Restaurant leaders have spent years training crews on the fundamentals of good service. AI doesn’t change those expectations. One finding in the 2026 QSR Drive-Thru Report caught my attention. In drive-thru visits where AI handled the order, mystery shoppers were 23.9 percentage points less likely to receive a thank-you at the pickup window. Positive assessments of crew demeanor were 15.7 percentage points lower. As someone who builds drive-thru AI, I think those numbers deserve a closer look. The study doesn’t tell us that AI caused those differences. And I don’t think the findings mean AI is inherently less hospitable than a human crew member. In some ways, AI has an advantage. It doesn’t get tired during the lunch rush or lose patience after answering the same question for the hundredth time. It can deliver the same friendly interaction on its five-hundredth order as it does on its first. But the findings do raise a question that restaurant operators and those of us building technology for them need to take seriously. We talk a lot about giving crews more time to focus on hospitality. What does that actually mean for someone juggling a dozen responsibilities during a lunch rush? The conversation doesn’t end at the speaker Before starting my company, I spent weeks standing near drive-thru order posts with a laptop, listening to hundreds of ordering conversations. I wanted to understand what actually happened between a guest pulling up to the speaker and placing an order. What struck me was how much crew members were juggling at once. They might be filling drinks, assembling orders or taking payments, all while taking orders through their headsets. And those orders weren’t always straightforward. Guests changed their minds, asked questions, made substitutions and occasionally ordered things that weren’t on the menu. Crew members had to keep up with every request, accurately enter orders into the point-of-sale system and make adjustments on the fly, all while keeping track of their other responsibilities. That’s where I see a real opportunity for AI. By handling the ordering conversation, AI can take one of those competing demands off a crew member’s plate. Crew members still wear headsets to monitor ordering conversations and step in when needed, but they no longer have to manage every exchange themselves. So, what does that mean for the guest? By the time they reach the pickup window, they may have spoken only to AI, and the crew member greeting them may not have participated in the ordering conversation at all. That doesn’t have to make the interaction less personal. With one less demand competing for their attention, crew members have an opportunity to make that first human exchange count. That could mean taking an extra moment to check that an order is complete, make sure food is packaged properly or explain a delay. Brands can also build a friendly greeting into their pickup-window scripts. And sometimes, it’s as simple as making eye contact, smiling and offering a genuine thank-you instead of hurriedly passing a bag through the window. There’s a benefit for the crew, too. Restaurant jobs are demanding, particularly during peak periods. Having one less conversation to manage while juggling other responsibilities can make a stressful shift a little more manageable. But none of these improvements is guaranteed simply because AI is taking orders. Better hospitality still takes intention Restaurant leaders have spent years training crews on the fundamentals of good service. AI doesn’t change those expectations. It creates an opportunity to help teams meet them more consistently. Making the most of that opportunity requires more than introducing the technology.
