Yum China Holdings, Inc. today announced that it has hit the 20,000-store milestone, spanning over 2,800 cities and towns across China, as it celebrates the 10th anniversary of its listing on the New York Stock Exchange. Yum China celebrates the 10th anniversary of its listing on the New York Stock Exchange The Company celebrated this milestone with over 10,000 restaurant general managers (RGMs) at its annual RGM convention. This year’s event was held in Chengdu, a vibrant city renowned for its rich culinary culture. The occasion was marked by the simultaneous opening of six new stores – one for each brand it operates in Mainland China: KFC, Pizza Hut, Lavazza, Taco Bell, Little Sheep and Huang Ji Huang. Joey Wat, CEO of Yum China, commented, “Reaching 20,000 stores is a milestone made possible by the hard work of Yum China employees and the trust of our customers. 2026 marks the second year of executing our RGM 3.0 strategy, which focuses on resilience, growth and moat. In a dynamic operating environment, we remain laser-focused on execution — solving problems, turning strategy into action, and delivering sustainable profitable growth.” Targeting 30,000 Stores by 2030 From the first KFC store in China, opened in 1987, it took the Company 33 years to reach its first 10,000 stores and just six years to add the next 10,000. As shared at its 2025 investor day, Yum China is targeting 30,000 stores by 2030, meaning it expects to add the next 10,000 stores within four years. This accelerated expansion underscores Yum China’s strong execution capabilities and significant runway for growth in China. The Company plans to continue expanding through its equity-and-franchise hybrid model, supported by diverse store formats and offerings tailored to different city tiers and consumer occasions. Alongside its rapid store expansion, KFC and Pizza Hut developed side-by-side modules including KCOFFEE café, KPRO and Pizza Hut Burger Bar, capturing new consumer occasions and generating incremental sales and profits. Through solid execution and a strong commitment to shareholder value, Yum China delivered double-digit diluted EPS growth year-over-year in the first nine months of this year and in each of the past three years, and continues to target a double-digit diluted EPS CAGR from 2026 to 2028, as outlined at its 2025 investor day. Since 2023, the Company has been exploring and deploying agentic AI to enhance operational efficiency across the organization. Its latest “AI Store Assistant” builds on Q-Smart and adds a range of new capabilities. By further integrating AI and advanced technologies with restaurant operating data and connected kitchen equipment, the upgraded agent provides real-time recommendations on operating decisions. Square today announced that Squaremates, an intelligent business agent that can take on complex, multi-step work across a seller’s business using its own secure workspace, is generally available to U.S. sellers¹. An evolution of Managerbot, Squaremates is the main way sellers experience Square Dashboard when they sign in: it’s where they ask questions, see what needs attention, and get work done. Alongside Squaremates, Square is also introducing an improved Square MCP (Model Context Protocol) and new Square CLI (Command-Line Interface), giving sellers and developers easy access to the Square platform, right within their own agentic tools – and the ability to build and host their own apps on Square with Squaremates Apps. “Running a business is an endless string of judgment calls that are all on the owner. How to price a new menu item, whether to add a shift, what to do about a slow week,” said Willem Avé, Square’s Global Head of Intelligence. “We built Squaremates to help share that load, and now it can take on more of the work than ever before: longer, more complex tasks that used to mean manual reconciliation and hours at a desk, now handled start to finish and handed back as something a seller can actually use. Square MCP and CLI further augment this vision. A lot of sellers already have an AI tool they like working in, and our job is to help that tool work directly with their Square business, so they can run things however’s most productive for them.” Richer Capabilities, More Time Back Managerbot launched in open beta six months ago, underpinned by two ideas: it monitors the business and proposes actions, while the seller decides; and it doesn’t just answer questions, it gets work done – all in service of helping sellers stay on top of what’s important and get time back to focus on what matters to them. Squaremates builds on that foundation, with access to cloud compute that lets it take on work spanning multiple steps or tasks and touching more parts of a business. For example, Squaremates can look at a period of sales, identify customers who have lapsed, and generate a marketing campaign or discount directed at bringing those customers back. It can review a seller’s catalog and make bulk updates across prices, descriptions, channel visibility, and even images. Or it can weigh labor costs against sales for a specified period and come back with a more cost-optimized staffing schedule to review. Squaremates also now creates rich artifacts when completing a task – usable outputs like a polished, graphical sales breakdown or a fully designed, on-brand email campaign rather than simply a block of text in a chat window. Squaremates’ reach is beginning to extend beyond Square itself. When it comes to restocking, a Squaremates capability currently in beta can check what’s running low, prepare an order, and build it directly on a supplier’s own site, ready for the seller to complete. And coming soon, a seller’s daily briefing will be able to pull in what’s waiting in their inbox alongside what’s happening in their business with permissioned access to their email account, giving sellers one place to start the day instead of several. The result: Squaremates can carry a task from start to finish, bring everything a seller needs into view before the day begins, and work directly with the third-party services sellers rely on to run their business, like suppliers, all while the seller decides what goes ahead. “Our cheese sauce is made in-house, and it’s gold. Bojangles is honoring America’s heroes by inviting guests to give back with every visit. From now through Dec. 13, participating Bojangles restaurants are raising funds for the Mae and George Siller Tunnel to Towers Foundation Scholarship Program, which provides scholarships for undergraduate degrees and accredited trade school programs to the children of Gold Star families, fallen first responders and catastrophically injured veterans and first responders. Depending on the restaurant, guests can support the campaign at checkout by rounding up their purchase, making a donation or doing both. Donors can give $1 or $5 and add their names to flags displayed in the restaurant, creating a visible show of community support. Those who donate $1 will receive a coupon for a free Bo-Berry Biscuit, and those who donate $5 will receive a coupon for a free Sausage Biscuit, both redeemable on their next visit. “Supporting military families is a cause close to our foundation’s heart,” said Ken Reynolds, Executive Director of the Bojangles Foundation. “This holiday season, we’re inviting our guests to help honor those who served by investing in their children’s futures, and every round-up and donation brings us closer to that goal.” “Our scholarship program carries the names of my parents, Mae and George Siller, who taught all seven of us that you take care of the people who take care of you,” said Frank Siller, Chairman and CEO of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation. “These children have already sacrificed more than anyone should have to. Thanks to Bojangles and its guests, every dollar raised this holiday season helps these children build the future they deserve. That’s what doing good looks like, and we are so grateful.” This is just the latest campaign in Bojangles’ ongoing commitment to supporting the military community, following its summer fundraiser in honor of America 250, in which the brand and its guests raised more than $519,000 for military families and veterans through Folds of Honor and the Veteran Golfers Association. The Tunnel to Towers campaign runs through Dec. 13 at participating Bojangles restaurants. For more information about Bojangles’ community impact, visit www.bojangles.com/foundation. articles.title: Starbucks is Putting More Money in Employees’ Pockets
articles.titleKo: Starbucks is Putting More Money in Employees’ Pockets
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Nearly 200,000 full- and part-time employees worldwide received new Bean Stock grants on Wednesday. Starbucks is giving hundreds of thousands of employees a financial stake in its turnaround, rolling out stock grants, performance bonuses, and expanded tipping opportunities as its Back to Starbucks strategy gains traction. The coffee giant announced Thursday that nearly 200,000 full- and part-time employees worldwide received new Bean Stock grants on Wednesday. Another 130,000 employees have stock grants from previous years vesting this month, continuing a program that has provided more than $2.75 billion in pretax gains since its introduction in 1991. More than 80 percent of eligible hourly employees in North America will receive their first payout Friday through the new Best of Starbucks Reward program. Announced earlier this spring, the initiative allows eligible baristas and shift supervisors to earn up to $300 each quarter when their coffeehouses meet or exceed certain sales, operational, and customer service metrics. Starbucks has also seen a substantial increase in customer tipping since expanding its digital tipping options in July. Customers have contributed more than $22 million in additional tips through the new channels, more than doubling tipping activity. Chief partner officer Sara Kelly and COO Mike Grams outlined the investments in a company blog post Thursday. “We have strong momentum in our Back to Starbucks plan, and coffeehouse partners are at the heart of that progress,” Kelly and Grams wrote. “Every day, they bring the Starbucks experience to life through their craft, the connections they create with customers, and the way they support one another.” The investments follow a strong fiscal fourth quarter for Starbucks, which reported its third consecutive quarter of U.S. same-store sales growth exceeding 7 percent. Domestic comps rose 7.7 percent, driven by a 2.4 percent increase in traffic and a 5.2 percent increase in average ticket. Global same-store sales climbed 7.2 percent, marking the company’s fifth consecutive quarter of worldwide growth. The stock grants continue a tradition that dates back 35 years, when Starbucks operated approximately 100 locations. The company became the first major retailer to offer stock grants to eligible full- and part-time hourly employees. Since the program began, more than 2 million employees have benefited from Bean Stock. Starbucks is also investing in staffing, scheduling, and its Green Apron Service initiative to improve daily operations. The company reported that hourly employee turnover is nearly half the industry average, and nearly 95 percent of employees receive their preferred schedules. More than 3 million people applied for jobs with Starbucks in North America last year. The chain is also maintaining its commitment to fill 90 percent of retail supervisory and managerial positions through internal promotions, creating advancement opportunities for existing employees. Other benefits available to eligible workers include comprehensive health coverage, full upfront tuition coverage for a first bachelor’s degree, and up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave. A recent study by Aon found that Starbucks offered more valuable benefits to hourly retail employees than any of the more than 60 U.S. companies examined. The compensation changes also consider unionized shops. Starbucks said the Best of Starbucks Reward, weekly pay, and expanded tipping options are subject to collective bargaining at the approximately 5 percent of its U.S. locations with union representation, as required by federal law. “When partners thrive, Starbucks thrives,” Kelly and Grams wrote. The post Starbucks is Putting More Money in Employees’ Pockets appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Mildreds Evolves Menu As The Plant-Based Pioneer Enters Its 38th Year
articles.titleKo: Mildreds Evolves Menu As The Plant-Based Pioneer Enters Its 38th Year
articles.originalSummary: London plant-based restaurant group Mildreds is evolving its menu this autumn, almost four decades after opening in Soho in 1988 – when dedicated vegetarian restaurants remained a relatively niche proposition. The new menu, launches across Mildreds’ five London restaurants, is the result of several months of development led by Food and Brand Director Sarah Wasserman and the group’s senior chef team. It builds on established Mildreds dishes while putting greater emphasis on vegetables, technique, provenance and the independent producers behind the food. The menu marks an evolution for the group, grown from its original Greek street restaurant to 5 locations across London; Soho, Camden, King’s Cross, Victoria and Covent Garden, moving from vegetarian to fully vegan cooking in 2021. Wasserman , who has spent over 20 years working in the Mildreds kitchen, said the development process focused on refining what the group does best. “This menu is the work of the whole kitchen team, not just me. I’ve spent over twenty years cooking at Mildreds, and if I’ve learned anything in that time, it’s that the best dishes come from patience, which is exactly how we built this menu: tested, changed and tested again, until we were happy to put our name to every one of them. It leans more on the people who grow what we cook with and the technique behind each dish, than anything we’ve done before.” The new menu includes Handmade Beetroot and Sweet Potato Tortelloni with Beetroot Velouté and Hazelnut Pistou ; Glazed Momo Dumplings with Chilli Miso, Cucumber and Ginger Pickle ; and Oyster Mushroom and Hispi Shawarma with Sweet Potato and Chipotle Romesco . Existing Mildreds dishes have been revisited rather than simply retained. Its Kiri hodi , one of the group’s best-known dishes, centres on roast squash, with biryani pilau, cabbage thoran and tomato and lime sambol. This is a menu that places produce at its centre, with dishes such as Sambal Mushrooms , Aubergine Milanese and Shiitake Whipped Tofu built around vegetables, pulses and technique. The menu has also been shaped by Mildreds’ supplier relationships, with independent producers providing key ingredients across the estate. Clean Bean Tofu, founded by Neil McLennan, supplies handmade London tofu made from organic soya beans. Suffolk producer Hodmedod’s provides British-grown pulses and grains, as well as fermented fava bean umami paste. Bread comes from Watford bakery Seven Seeded , whose sourdough is made using four ingredients and fermented for 48 hours. Belazu supplies olive oil and Mediterranean ingredients, working with the Pons family of olive growers in Catalonia, while plant-based products from Symplicity bring traditional fermentation techniques into the kitchen. The wider pantry is supported by Brighton workers’ co-operative Infinity Foods , which has traded since 1971, while seasonal fruit and vegetables, including pumpkins and squash used extensively on the new menu, are sourced through Wild Harvest’s network of UK and European growers. Drinks follow a similar approach, with coffee from Cornwall-based Origin , tea from Rare Tea Co and wine supplied by family merchant Ellis Wines , which dates back to 1822. The bar range includes independent producers such as El Tequileño, Sapling Vodka and Jaisalmer Gin. Managing Director Sam Anstey said: “Mildreds has helped lead the way in vegetarian and vegan dining in London since 1988. Our focus has always been on serving food that people want to come back for, whether they are vegan, vegetarian or simply love good food. This menu builds on that reputation, with bold flavours, great ingredients and the care and skill of Sarah and our kitchen team.”

articles.title: Smithdown Road Favourite ‘The Tavern Co’ Opens in Liverpool City Centre with Tavern Co Social on Water Street
articles.titleKo: Smithdown Road Favourite ‘The Tavern Co’ Opens in Liverpool City Centre with Tavern Co Social on Water Street
articles.originalSummary: One of Liverpool’s most celebrated independent culinary institutions has arrived in the heart of the city centre. The team behind the multi-award-winning The Tavern Co on Smithdown Road has opened its new concept, Tavern Co Social, on Water Street. Taking over the prominent ground-floor site inside the historic New Zealand House – the former home of Hooters and the legendary Newz Bar – the venue brings fresh, modern energy to one of the city’s most iconic streets. For over three decades, The Tavern Co has been a cornerstone of Liverpool’s independent food scene, twice named the home of the “UK’s Best Breakfast” for its legendary full English and American-style morning spreads. Now, the brand has brought its community-focused ethos, established reputation and famous flavours to a wider city-centre audience. Tavern Co Social blends the nostalgic, welcoming charm of the original Wavertree landmark with a high-energy, modern social space. By day, guests can enjoy the iconic breakfast and brunch menus that built the brand’s following. As evening approaches, the 120-cover venue transitions into an intimate, lively social hub featuring a specialised tapas menu, craft beers, hearty dishes and a dedicated setup for sports enthusiasts. The space features a sleek, contemporary interior anchored by an expansive main bar, complete with more than 10 TVs positioned throughout the venue so sports fans can catch every major event from plush booths or right at the bar. This expansion marks a significant milestone for the brand under its new ownership group, which has invested heavily in modernising and securing the future of the flagship South Liverpool site since 2023. The second location represents a major vote of confidence in Liverpool’s commercial district and daytime hospitality market. Mellissa Dunleavy, General Manager of Tavern Co Social, said: “For over three decades, The Tavern Co has been a staple of Liverpool’s food scene on Smithdown Road, famous for bringing people together. Expanding into Liverpool city centre is a massive milestone for us. This new site will create over 20 full- and part-time jobs for the industry while bringing an iconic building back to life. We look forward to welcoming familiar faces from our heritage site, as well as new diners trying out Tavern 2.0 for the first time.” Tavern Co Social opened on Friday 18 September 2026 and operates daily from 8:00am. articles.title: 5 Lessons from John Peyton on Dine’s Dual-Brand Bet
articles.titleKo: 5 Lessons from John Peyton on Dine’s Dual-Brand Bet
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Applebee's-IHOP approach has runway for hundreds of locations. Nobody asked Dine Brands to put Applebee’s and IHOP under one roof. But according to CEO John Peyton, guests are finding plenty to like once they walk through the door: Two-thirds of checks at the company’s dual-brand restaurants include items from both menus. For Peyton, that illustrates an important distinction between responding to demand and creating something customers couldn’t quite picture beforehand. On FSR’s Restaurant Innovator podcast, he discusses how the format grew from international experimentation into a U.S. development opportunity. With 60 locations open and more on the way, the effort offers lessons that extend beyond pairing two familiar names. LISTEN TO THE FULL EPISODE HERE 1. Look for complementary demand, not just compatible brands The logic behind combining Applebee’s and IHOP starts with when people visit. IHOP brings breakfast strength. Applebee’s brings an established afternoon and evening business. Together, they create an opportunity to generate more sales from an existing building throughout the day. For IHOP operators, that means addressing a historically challenging dinner business. For Applebee’s franchisees, it means adding a breakfast occasion they weren’t serving. That distinction matters as operators contend with higher costs. Peyton sees adding an entire daypart as a different growth proposition from competing for another incremental visit. Most locations have been conversions, allowing franchisees to spread fixed costs across more sales. “That incremental revenue flows at a higher margin than the original restaurant because the fixed costs remain the same,” he says. READ MORE: Dine Brands Looks to Find New Ways to Win at Applebee’s and IHOP 2. Give customers something concrete to react to Peyton argues that a focus group would have struggled to evaluate a shared Applebee’s–IHOP experience without seeing it. Dine Brands wasn’t starting without evidence. International operators had already opened dual-brand restaurants, and Peyton visited locations before pursuing the opportunity domestically. But translating that evidence into a U.S. concept required franchisees willing to open restaurants before every detail was settled. Those early operators understood they would help refine the format as they learned what worked. “We had conversations with the first franchisees that the concept you open is not going to necessarily be the concept in two years, and together we’re going to refine it and tweak it,” Peyton says. “And so we went big and we went all in.” Research followed the experience rather than substituting for it. With restaurants operating, Dine could ask guests what they liked, what needed improvement, and how their impressions changed after visiting. One early finding: Guests largely don’t care which brand’s side they sit on, provided they can order from both menus. “One of the definitions of innovation is giving the consumer something they didn’t know they wanted,” Peyton says. Combine the experience without doubling the complexity Putting two brands together could easily mean giving the kitchen twice as much to manage. Dine Brands deliberately avoided that approach. While overseas locations had essentially combined both menus, the U.S. team streamlined the offering to keep the total item count in line with an individual brand’s menu. Overlapping products underwent a comparison process. The resulting burger, for example, uses an Applebee’s burger and an IHOP bun. Still, menu editing doesn’t eliminate the learning curve. articles.title: Your 3rd Spot Bolsters Leadership Bench Ahead of Multimarket Expansion
articles.titleKo: Your 3rd Spot Bolsters Leadership Bench Ahead of Multimarket Expansion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . AMP Up1 Hospitality is readying its roster as it prepares for the next phase of growth. In late October, the experiential dining and entertainment company behind Your 3rd Spot and forthcoming concept The Looking Glass announced three senior leadership appointments. The group promoted Chris Barrows to chief operating officer, Erin Callahan to senior vice president of operations and managing partner overseeing the Midwest, and hired Atlanta chef Joe Schafer as culinary director and executive chef. The leadership moves arrive as AMP Up1 is building The Looking Glass , an immersive social playground designed to accommodate more than 1,000 guests, set to open in downtown Atlanta in spring 2027 . Plus, the team is expanding Your 3rd Spot to a second location at Veridian—a 225-acre mixed-use development in Schaumburg, Illinois—in 2028. For founder and chief vision officer Josh Rossmeisl, the appointments are about building the operating teams and culinary capabilities needed to support those ambitions. “We’re thinking about the company we want to become, not just the one we’re operating today,” he tells FSR . “Great real estate, access to capital, and incredible ideas are all important, but ultimately, the success of our brands will be determined by the people we surround ourselves with.” “You can’t wait until you’re ready to open the next location to start building that leadership foundation,” he adds. From Hourly Employees to the C-Suite Barrows is stepping into the COO role after serving as AMP Up1’s chief people officer, bringing nearly two decades of experience in operations and talent development. Previously chief people officer, Chris Barrows now takes responsibility for company operations, developing leaders, and maintaining consistent standards as the company builds additional venues. His hospitality career began in 2007 as a host at Kings Dining & Entertainment in Boston, where he met Rossmeisl . A Georgia State University graduate with a degree in managerial sciences, Barrows advanced through floor management, assistant general manager, and general manager positions before taking on companywide responsibilities in systems, training, recruiting, and talent development. “Starting as a host taught me that the opportunity in front of you matters more than the destination you can’t control yet,” Barrows says. “I took a pay cut to be around the right people and situation. I didn’t have grand end goals, but I bet on myself to do a good job and a find a way to be successful. That decision has shaped everything since.” His advice to leaders in similar situations? “Stop fixating on where you’re going and do something with where you are. The next rep leads to the next opportunity,” he says. “That’s still how I think about growth and leadership today. The opportunities that ending came weren’t there when I started, and I like to believe that the work created them. When they came, I was ready.” As a member of AMP Up1’s founding leadership team, he helped build the recruiting practices, training programs, and leadership development systems supporting Your 3rd Spot’s Atlanta debut. His expanded responsibilities now include company operations, leadership development, and maintaining consistent standards as the portfolio grows. The promotion also puts an internal development story at the center of the company’s expansion: a former hourly employee is now responsible for leading its operations. That employee-first philosophy is baked into the company’s DNA. At the heart of the group’s success and future outlook is an innovative approach to team empowerment—one that grants employees a genuine stake in the company’s success. articles.title: Comerciários de SP e RS fecham acordo para reduzir a escala 6×1 para 5×2
articles.titleKo: Comerciários de SP e RS fecham acordo para reduzir a escala 6×1 para 5×2
articles.originalSummary: Os sindicatos dos comerciários de São Paulo e de Porto Alegre firmaram acordos coletivos e aditivos com representantes do setor empresarial para viabilizar o fim da escala 6×1 a partir de dezembro, conforme previsto na Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) 141. A negociação ocorre mesmo após a Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC) protocolar, no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), uma ação direta de inconstitucionalidade, com pedido de medida cautelar . A entidade buscava adiar a implementação da mudança para dezembro de 2027. Com os novos acordos, cerca de 700 mil trabalhadores de São Paulo e Porto Alegre serão afetados. A emenda à Constituição que acaba com a escala 6×1 foi promulgada em 16 de outubro pelo Congresso. A sessão contou com a participação do presidente Lula (PT), que tinha na proposta uma de suas bandeiras na campanha à reeleição. Acordos são válidos a partir de 16 de dezembro O presidente do Sindicato dos Comerciários de São Paulo, Ricardo Patah, afirmou que a adoção da escala 5×2 e a redução da jornada de trabalho para 42 horas semanais entram em vigor em 16 de dezembro. Entre os setores atingidos na capital paulista estão supermercados, atacado, carnes, calçados, automóveis e aço. “O movimento sindical não quer quebrar as empresas ou enfraquecer a saúde financeira delas. Pelo contrário, vamos trabalhar conjuntamente e buscaremos valorizar o ser humano, que terá a oportunidade efetiva de ter um dia a mais com a sua família, se qualificar ou fazer o que achar melhor”, disse. O acordo na cidade de São Paulo autoriza formatos flexíveis como 5×2 e 4×3, além de bancos de horas compensatórios, proibindo a escala 6×1 tradicional. Já o Sindicato dos Empregados no Comércio de Porto Alegre (Sindec-POA) informou que o acordo abrange cerca de 100 mil trabalhadores, 22 sindicatos patronais e 30 mil estabelecimentos na capital gaúcha. Na cidade, a partir de 16 dezembro de 2026, a jornada será reduzida de 44 horas para 42h semanais, distribuídas em cinco dias de trabalho. Já em dezembro de 2027, haverá novamente a redução da carga horária, chegando a 40 horas semanais, sem redução salarial. Antecipação das folgas em Porto Alegre Em Porto Alegre, a partir de 1º de dezembro deste ano, será instituído um banco de descanso remunerado. Nas semanas de pico de vendas que antecedem o Natal e o Ano Novo, iniciadas nos dias 14, 21 e 28, os trabalhadores terão direito a duas folgas remuneradas. Nilton Neco Souza da Silva, presidente do Sindec-POA, afirmou que um destes descansos deverá ser usufruído na própria semana, enquanto o outro poderá ser utilizado em outros dias de dezembro. “Só precisa garantir que o trabalhador tenha as 8 folgas durante o mês. A grande vantagem é que a empresa poderá antecipá-las a partir de 1º de dezembro”, explicou. Para ele, a medida representa um avanço significativo, ao contemplar tanto os trabalhadores, que dependem das comissões durante as festas de fim de ano, quanto os empregadores, que buscam manter as lojas em funcionamento com o quadro completo de funcionários. “A partir de janeiro de 2027, a empresa poderá adotar a escala 6×1 em uma das semanas, se garantir as oito folgas ao longo do mês. Assim, poderá alternar semanas de 5×2 e 4×3, facilitando a organização em períodos de maior movimento no comércio”, disse. Segundo Silva, a negociação, embora exitosa para ambos os lados, foi concluída em apenas duas semanas. “Isso prova haver tempo, sim, para firmar um acordo, desmontando o argumento da CNI (Confederação Nacional da Indústria) e da CNC de que isso não seria possível e de que, por isso, seria necessário adiar a mudança para dezembro do próximo ano. Há, sim, a possibilidade de construir um acordo que beneficie a todos”, afirmou. Dino decidirá regras até sexta-feira O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), disse que vai proferir uma decisão até esta sexta-feira, 13, para remover “amarras” e facilitar a negociação coletiva na implementação do fim da esc

articles.title: Shopee registra alta de 90% nas vendas na semana que antecede o 11.11
articles.titleKo: Shopee registra alta de 90% nas vendas na semana que antecede o 11.11
articles.originalSummary: A Shopee registrou crescimento de 90% no volume de vendas entre 5 e 10 de novembro, na comparação com os dias que antecederam a Black Friday de 2025. O resultado foi impulsionado pela procura por produtos de maior ticket médio, como smartphones, televisores, geladeiras, freezers e scooters, segundo a plataforma. Entre os itens sazonais, ar-condicionado e artigos de decoração natalina também ganharam destaque, com árvores de Natal e piscas-piscas entre os produtos mais buscados. “Estamos prontos para tornar o 11.11 deste ano o nosso maior dia de vendas da história da Shopee no País. Esses resultados revelam uma prévia de como os brasileiros aproveitam as oportunidades de economia no mês de maior expectativa para o varejo. Temos uma programação que conecta todo o nosso ecossistema, com benefícios, entretenimento e dezenas de milhares de ofertas em mais de 30 categorias, além de cupons especiais e entrega rápida”, afirma Felipe Piringer, diretor de Marketing da Shopee. O movimento acompanha a intenção de compra dos consumidores: 86% planejam comprar durante o 11.11 e/ou a Black Friday, de acordo com pesquisa da Shopee. Nas primeiras horas do 11.11, a plataforma registrou crescimento superior a 40% no número de acessos, impulsionado por R$ 25 milhões em cupons de desconto e vouchers de frete grátis sem valor mínimo de compra. O ticket médio por produto avançou 18% em relação às primeiras horas da Black Friday de 2025. As categorias com maior destaque foram Casa, Eletrônicos, Beleza, Esportes e Lazer e Casa & Construção. O Pix foi a forma de pagamento escolhida por 52% dos consumidores, enquanto o cartão de crédito respondeu por 35% das transações. articles.titleKo: Serviços recuam 0,1% em setembro; 10 especialistas alertam para risco de estagnação em 2027
articles.originalSummary: O setor de serviços, responsável pela maior parcela dos empregos da economia brasileira, registrou variação de -0,1% em setembro , na comparação com agosto, segundo dados da Pesquisa Mensal de Serviços (PMS), divulgada pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ). O resultado foi influenciado principalmente pelas atividades de transportes e de informação e comunicação. Na comparação anual, o setor também apresentou recuo de 0,1%, interrompendo uma sequência de 29 resultados positivos em relação ao mesmo mês do ano anterior. Para o IBGE, variações dessa magnitude são consideradas estabilidade. Confira a análise de 10 especialistas sobre os desafios do setor de serviços e os riscos de estagnação em 2027. Lucas Minucci, professor da PIB The New College O setor de serviços continua relevante para a geração de empregos, mas a manutenção desse desempenho dependerá de maior eficiência empresarial. Juros elevados, inflação e incertezas internacionais exigem planejamento financeiro e adaptação. Para sustentar o crescimento, as empresas precisarão aumentar a produtividade, investir na formação de lideranças e integrar finanças, tecnologia e estratégia, sem depender exclusivamente da ampliação das equipes. Sidney Lima, analista da Ouro Preto Investimentos A perda de força dos serviços indica que os efeitos da política monetária restritiva estão se espalhando pela economia. O emprego e a renda ainda sustentam parte do consumo, mas famílias demonstram menor disposição para gastar e empresas, para investir. A combinação de crescimento mais fraco e inflação de serviços resistente pode levar o Banco Central a manter os juros elevados por mais tempo. Sem estabilidade fiscal, melhores condições de crédito e recuperação da confiança dos investidores, a economia pode entrar em 2027 com menor dinamismo. O faturamento nominal, por outro lado, cresceu 6,4% em um ano, indicando pressão de preços mesmo com o volume praticamente estagnado. Entre os riscos para 2027 estão juros elevados, endividamento das famílias e aumento dos custos operacionais. A tendência é de crescimento moderado, caso não haja avanços na política fiscal que permitam reduzir os juros. Gustavo Assis, CEO da Asset A sustentação dos serviços depende de condições financeiras mais favoráveis. A persistência da inflação, as incertezas fiscais e o custo do crédito estão entre os principais riscos para a atividade. Para transformar a recuperação em crescimento duradouro, será necessário ampliar a produtividade, recuperar a confiança empresarial e estimular investimentos. No primeiro semestre, informação e comunicação avançaram 8%, ante 1,8% do conjunto dos serviços. A digitalização pode ampliar a produtividade, mas o crescimento não deve depender exclusivamente do consumo. Nesse cenário, o venture capital pode financiar startups que desenvolvam soluções para reduzir custos, aumentar a competitividade e impulsionar novos mercados. articles.title: WeWork libera 23 unidades no Brasil para aluguel de espaços por hora
articles.titleKo: WeWork libera 23 unidades no Brasil para aluguel de espaços por hora
articles.originalSummary: A busca por maior flexibilidade no uso dos espaços corporativos está abrindo novas possibilidades para o mercado de escritórios compartilhados. A WeWork lançou o serviço On Demand em 53 unidades na América Latina, permitindo que profissionais e empresas reservem mesas de trabalho e salas de reunião por períodos que vão de meia hora a um dia inteiro. No Brasil, o serviço está disponível em 23 unidades localizadas em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Belo Horizonte e Porto Alegre. A iniciativa também contempla Colômbia, México, Peru, Argentina e Chile. As reservas podem ser feitas pelo aplicativo móvel da WeWork ou pelo site da empresa. A contratação permite pagar apenas pelo período utilizado. No caso das mesas de trabalho, a reserva por um dia dá acesso às áreas comuns da unidade, incluindo cabines privativas e espaços de descanso. Já as salas de reunião podem ser alugadas por hora. O lançamento ocorre em um cenário de mudanças na relação dos profissionais com o escritório. Segundo o estudo “A experiência laboral de 2026 no Brasil”, realizado pela WeWork em parceria com a Offerwise, 79% dos entrevistados afirmam que a ida ao escritório é uma exigência do empregador, e não uma escolha. Se pudessem decidir, apenas 42% optariam pelo trabalho presencial. “As empresas continuam precisando de espaço e demandam cada vez mais. O que mudou foi a maneira de usá-lo”, afirma Claudio Hidalgo, presidente da WeWork para a América Latina. Com o On Demand, a WeWork busca atender profissionais que precisam de um local de trabalho ou de reunião pontualmente, sem assumir compromissos de longo prazo. A plataforma também permite que usuários brasileiros reservem espaços em mais de 300 unidades da empresa, distribuídas por 70 cidades no mundo. A companhia mantém 69 unidades na América Latina. Segundo Hidalgo, a operação regional é lucrativa em todas as localidades há mais de um ano, com taxa de ocupação superior a 80%. Para o executivo, a flexibilização do trabalho também exige uma revisão do papel do escritório nas empresas. A tendência, segundo ele, é substituir a presença baseada no controle por uma dinâmica orientada a objetivos e confiança, na qual o deslocamento até o ambiente corporativo esteja associado a uma finalidade específica. A Wework afirma que seguirá concentrada na consolidação da operação e na rentabilidade do negócio na região, ampliando modelos de uso flexível dos espaços. The military initiative builds on CPK’s broader automated retail strategy to implement and operate up to 1,000 automated retail machines nationwide over the next three years. In recognition of the men and women who serve our nation, California Pizza Kitchen (CPK) today announced an initiative to bring its signature California-inspired pizzas directly to U.S. military installations through a phased deployment of automated pizza kiosks. Partnering with Ranger Group and its CEO, U.S. Army Ranger veteran, Mark “Ranger” Jones, CPK plans to roll out hundreds of automated pizza machines across installations serving the U.S. Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and U.S. Coast Guard, with planned placements at bases across America. The military initiative builds on CPK’s broader automated retail strategy to implement and operate up to 1,000 automated retail machines nationwide over the next three years, bringing restaurant-quality CPK favorites to airports, universities, hospitals and other high-traffic locations. The machines use Turbo-chef powered cooking and touch-screen technology to deliver a freshly baked CPK pizza in as little as 90 seconds. The deployment to U.S. military installations extends that same on-demand, restaurant-quality experience to the service members who work and train on base. The initiative expands CPK’s presence beyond traditional restaurants and grocery store shelves, bringing the brand’s distinctive approach to pizza directly to the places where America’s military personnel work and train. Designed to provide convenient access to hot and fresh pizza, the machines will offer service members a high-quality and convenient meal option while on base or at sea. “As a veteran myself, I’m personally proud to bring our restaurant-quality pizzas directly to the places where our service members work and train,” said Michael Beacham, President of California Pizza Kitchen Global. “This initiative is both an expression of our gratitude and a meaningful step forward in our mission to make the California Pizza Kitchen experience more accessible wherever people are.” Bringing Great Pizza Closer to Those Who Serve The military deployment program combines CPK’s recognized brand and culinary heritage with automated foodservice technology designed for high-demand environments. Ranger Group will work with CPK and military stakeholders to coordinate and facilitate the phased deployment, including installation logistics and ongoing operational support. “As a former U.S. Army Ranger, I know how much a great meal made with quality ingredients can mean to service members and their families after a long day of training or duty,” said Mark “Ranger” Jones, CEO of Ranger Group. “This partnership with California Pizza Kitchen is personal to me. We are bringing an iconic American brand to the places where military personnel and their families work, live and serve, giving them convenient access to quality food and showing our appreciation for their sacrifice. It is an honor to help make this happen.” A New Frontier for California Pizza Kitchen The military initiative is part of CPK’s broader strategy to expand access to its signature pizzas through innovative, non-traditional dining formats. By extending the brand into locations where traditional restaurant development may not be practical, CPK is creating new opportunities to serve consumers in workplaces, transportation hubs, educational institutions and other high-traffic environments. The military rollout will proceed in phases, beginning with domestic installations and potentially expanding to additional military locations, including overseas facilities, in the future. For CPK, the initiative reflects a simple belief: great pizza should be available wherever people live, work and gather — including the men and women who dedicate their lives to serving the United State

articles.title: Vendas do varejo caem 4% em outubro e registram pior resultado para o mês desde 2023
articles.titleKo: Vendas do varejo caem 4% em outubro e registram pior resultado para o mês desde 2023
articles.originalSummary: As vendas do varejo brasileiro caíram 4,0% em outubro de 2026 em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025, já descontada a inflação, segundo o Índice Cielo do Varejo Ampliado (ICVA). O resultado representa o pior desempenho para o mês de outubro desde 2023, quando a retração foi de 4,1%. O faturamento real ficou abaixo do registrado um ano antes pelo 17º mês consecutivo. A sequência de recuos começou em junho de 2025, mas perdeu intensidade em relação a setembro , quando as vendas ficaram 4,2% abaixo do nível de um ano antes. Duráveis e serviços têm as maiores quedas As vendas de bens duráveis e semiduráveis recuaram 8,9%. Óticas e joalherias e lojas de materiais de construção estiveram entre os segmentos que mais contribuíram para o resultado negativo. Em serviços , a retração foi de 8,5%, puxada principalmente por turismo e transporte, além de autopeças e serviços automotivos. Os bens não duráveis registraram a menor retração entre os três grupos, de 0,7%. Nessa categoria, o varejo alimentício especializado se destacou pelo desempenho positivo, enquanto livrarias, papelarias e afins deram a maior contribuição negativa. Centro-Oeste tem maior retração regional O faturamento real recuou nas cinco regiões do País. O Centro-Oeste teve a maior retração (5,4%), seguido pelo Sudeste (5,2%), Nordeste (3,5%) e Norte (2,3%). O Sul registrou a menor queda (0,8%), com crescimento no Paraná (0,7%) e em Santa Catarina (0,1%). Entre os Estados, o Amapá liderou as altas (2,4%), seguido por Rondônia (1,2%) e Acre (0,8%). Na outra ponta, São Paulo teve o pior resultado, com recuo de 6,4%, à frente de Goiás (6,3%) e Rio Grande do Norte (5,6%). Varejo físico e e-commerce têm resultados distintos O faturamento nominal do e-commerce recuou 0,5% em outubro de 2026, na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025, segundo o ICVA. No varejo físico, as vendas cresceram 1,9% no período. Os dois resultados refletem a variação da receita de vendas antes do desconto da inflação. O IPCA-15 subiu 0,3% em outubro, abaixo da alta de 0,7% registrada em setembro. Em 12 meses, o indicador acumulou avanço de 4,6%. Dos nove grupos pesquisados, oito apresentaram aumento de preços no período. Alimentação e bebidas registrou a maior alta entre os grupos, de 0,9%, acelerando ante 0,4% em setembro. A alimentação no domicílio subiu 1,0%, também acima da variação de 0,4% do mês anterior. Já a alimentação fora do domicílio aumentou 0,6%, ante 0,4% em setembro. Em Transportes, os preços avançaram 0,1%, com alta de 1,2% nos combustíveis, enquanto as passagens aéreas recuaram 9,2%. Habitação teve queda de 0,1%, influenciada pela redução de 0,9% na energia elétrica residencial, associada à mudança para a bandeira tarifária verde. Assim, embora a inflação geral tenha desacelerado em outubro, a alta mais forte dos alimentos pode ter pressionado o orçamento das famílias. O contexto ajuda a explicar o contraste entre o crescimento nominal de 1,3% e a queda real de 4,0% do ICVA, mas não permite atribuir o desempenho do varejo exclusivamente à inflação. articles.title: Temu e Correios firmam acordo para ampliar operações logísticas no Brasil
articles.titleKo: Temu e Correios firmam acordo para ampliar operações logísticas no Brasil
articles.originalSummary: A Temu assinou um Memorando de Entendimento (MOU, na sigla em inglês) com os Correios para ampliar a cooperação em logística e comércio eletrônico no Brasil. O acordo prevê a avaliação de novas soluções de entrega e serviços logísticos para empresas brasileiras que comercializam produtos por meio do Programa de Vendedores Locais da plataforma. A parceria poderá utilizar a capilaridade e a infraestrutura dos Correios para ampliar as opções de entrega e oferecer suporte aos vendedores que atuam no marketplace. A iniciativa também faz parte da estratégia da Temu de fortalecer sua operação no Brasil por meio de parcerias com empresas e prestadores de serviços locais. “Construir relações sólidas com parceiros locais é uma parte importante da nossa atuação nos mercados em que estamos presentes. A parceria com os Correios busca facilitar a experiência logística dos consumidores e, ao mesmo tempo, oferecer mais suporte aos vendedores locais para que possam expandir seus negócios online”, afirma a empresa. Segundo Emmanoel Schmidt Rondon, presidente dos Correios , o acordo abre novas oportunidades de negócios e reforça o papel da estatal como parceira logística do comércio eletrônico no País. A colaboração combina a presença nacional da empresa com a atuação da plataforma no mercado digital. A Temu iniciou suas operações no Brasil em junho de 2024 e lançou, em setembro de 2025, seu Programa de Vendedores Locais, que permite a empresas brasileiras utilizar a plataforma como canal de vendas para alcançar consumidores e ampliar sua presença no comércio eletrônico. Com a aproximação, a empresa busca fortalecer a estrutura logística oferecida aos vendedores brasileiros à medida que expandem seus negócios no ambiente digital. articles.title: Produção de veículos no Brasil sobe 2,7% em outubro ante outubro de 2025, diz Anfavea
articles.titleKo: Produção de veículos no Brasil sobe 2,7% em outubro ante outubro de 2025, diz Anfavea
articles.originalSummary: A produção de veículos subiu 2,7% em outubro, ante o mesmo mês de 2025, refletindo a perda de tração das vendas no mercado doméstico e um resultado considerado preocupante das exportações. No total, foram montadas 254,5 mil unidades, entre carros de passeio, utilitários leves, caminhões e ônibus. O volume ficou 5,1% abaixo do registrado em setembro. Divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 11, pela Anfavea , a entidade que representa as montadoras, o balanço mostra que, desde o início do ano, foram montados 2,42 milhões de veículos, o que corresponde a um crescimento de 8% ante os dez primeiros meses do ano passado. Vendas de veículos perdem fôlego Em outubro, as vendas de veículos no Brasil somaram 265,5 mil unidades. Na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025, o crescimento foi de 1,8%. Ante setembro, as vendas encolheram 5,6%, indicando perda de fôlego do mercado. Exportações de veículos recuam quase 30% Já as exportações, de 29,1 mil veículos em outubro, recuaram 28,3% na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025. Na margem, ou seja, ante setembro, os embarques recuaram 26,9%. No acumulado desde janeiro, as exportações agora recuam 23,5%, somando 363,1 mil veículos em dez meses. Perda de espaço no mercado externo A Anfavea classificou como “preocupantes” os resultados no comércio exterior, apontando perda de participação das montadoras do Brasil em mercados vizinhos, sobretudo para produtos provenientes da Ásia e do México. Além disso, a Argentina, principal destino das exportações brasileiras, também enfrenta retração do mercado interno, o que afeta diretamente os embarques nacionais de automóveis. Montadoras ampliam quadro de funcionários O balanço da entidade mostra ainda que as montadoras abriram 467 vagas de trabalho em outubro. As fábricas de veículos agora empregam 116,3 mil pessoas. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Daniel Tozzi e Eduardo Laguna). articles.title: How Restaurants Can Capture the Market While Competitors Give Up Ground
articles.titleKo: How Restaurants Can Capture the Market While Competitors Give Up Ground
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . When other restaurants in the area go quiet on local marketing channels, two things happen simultaneously: ad costs soften, and noise drops. Restaurant operators reported a net decline in customer traffic in 19 of the last 20 months, according to the National Restaurant Association . The same trend is reflected in the slowdown of new jobs in restaurants and bars from 31,500 in August to just 11,000 in September . Such indicators, together with persistent political and economic uncertainty, make the instinct to batten down the hatches, trim the marketing budget and wait out the storm fully understandable. It’s also one of the most expensive decisions a restaurant can make. When Harvard Business Review researchers studied 4,700 public companies across three recessions, only about 9 percent emerged outperforming their rivals by at least 10 percent in sales and profit growth. The approach most likely to land a company in that group was not being conservative. It was pairing operational discipline with greater investment in marketing and development. This is the same principle that led Harvard Professor John Quelch to write in 2008 that maintaining marketing spend through the recession could increase market share at lower costs than otherwise possible. Here are the investments that restaurant operators can prioritize to take advantage when competitors go on the defensive. 1. Fill the Channels Competitors Abandon When other restaurants in the area go quiet on local marketing channels, two things happen simultaneously: ad costs soften, and noise drops. An operator that merely holds marketing spend in that moment can purchase more representation on TV, social platforms, maps, radio and the like at a time when the total volume of ads is decreasing. Their share of voice (SOV), or their percentage of the market’s total advertising noise, increases without the need for any additional investment. And the gap between SOV and share of market, known as excess share of voice (ESOV), just so happens to be one of the strongest predictors of long-term share growth. An analysis of the IPA Effectiveness Databank covering the 2008–09 recession found that brands with ESOV above 8 points saw 4.5 times the annual market share growth of brands with zero or negative ESOV. Restaurants that can afford to increase their spending during a slowdown can maximize the SOV they win during the discount and the advantage they’ll have when demand returns. 2. Break Into New Markets The advantages of discounted SOV don’t have to end with a restaurant’s traditional target audience. The same equation that lets restaurants claim a bigger share of their primary market also lowers the cost of entry in adjacent markets. When competitors stop advertising their offerings in catering, private events or a neighboring suburb, establishing a new name in those spaces becomes significantly cheaper. Expansions that were too high-risk in a strong market start to make sense under these conditions. Careful digital marketing practice reduces the downside further by allowing operators to test new audiences at a minimal upfront cost before pursuing the ones that show positive feedback. 3. Keep the Test Kitchen Running Menu and concept development run on long lead times. A new prototype, a beverage program or a retooled menu can take many months to move from the test kitchen to the dining room, so cuts made today create gaps that surface in what may be a very different market. An operator who keeps development running while competitors shut down the test kitchen will be able to debut their innovations in a relatively unsaturated and potentially high-demand environment. By the time the competitors start investing in their own development programs once more, they’ll find themselves a full cycle behind. As always, development should be informed by guest data. articles.title: Reforma tributária: governo apresentará texto para facilitar adaptação
articles.titleKo: Reforma tributária: governo apresentará texto para facilitar adaptação
articles.originalSummary: O governo federal vai encaminhar ao Congresso Nacional uma proposta para criar uma regra de transição na cobrança da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), novo tributo federal da reforma tributária. A medida permitirá que as empresas façam um cálculo estimado do imposto nos primeiros meses de vigência do sistema e realizem ajustes posteriormente, reduzindo dificuldades na adaptação às novas regras. O anúncio foi feito nesta quarta-feira, 11, pelo secretário especial da Receita Federal , Robinson Barreirinhas, durante coletiva de imprensa sobre o Programa de Conformidade da Reforma Tributária, no Ministério da Fazenda. Segundo o secretário, a proposta busca dar mais segurança aos contribuintes durante a migração para o modelo de crédito vinculado ao pagamento e para o sistema de split payment – mecanismo que vincula o aproveitamento de créditos tributários ao efetivo recolhimento do tributo na operação. “Para tranquilizar e ter certeza absoluta de que ninguém vai ter problema nessa transição, nós vamos propor para o Congresso Nacional uma regra opcional”, afirmou o secretário. Pela sistemática apresentada, as empresas passarão a emitir documentos fiscais dentro das novas regras a partir de janeiro de 2027. Na primeira apuração da CBS, prevista para fevereiro, o contribuinte poderá calcular o tributo com base em uma estimativa dos créditos a que terá direito. Eventuais diferenças serão ajustadas na apuração do mês seguinte. De acordo com Barreirinhas, o mecanismo funcionará como uma alternativa para contribuintes que ainda estejam se adaptando às novas regras de aproveitamento de créditos tributários. “Até que o split payment esteja totalmente implementado, principalmente nas operações entre empresas, esse modelo pode funcionar como mecanismo de transição”, disse. Regulamentação Ao defender a entrada em vigor da reforma dentro do cronograma previsto pelo governo, o secretário afirmou que a regulamentação vem sendo construída em diálogo com Estados, municípios, entidades empresariais e profissionais da contabilidade. Segundo ele, a primeira versão do regulamento recebeu quase 5 mil sugestões de aperfeiçoamento, que foram analisadas pela Receita Federal e pelos demais órgãos envolvidos na implementação. “Todas as decisões da reforma precisam ser tomadas por consenso. Isso demanda um diálogo institucional muito forte”, afirmou. Barreirinhas informou que uma nova versão do regulamento deverá ser publicada nos próximos dias e destacou que o trabalho continuará após a publicação das normas complementares previstas para este ano. Créditos para investimentos O secretário também destacou os efeitos que a reforma poderá trazer para os investimentos produtivos . Pelas novas regras, os tributos pagos na compra de máquinas, equipamentos, imóveis e outros bens de capital passarão a gerar créditos imediatos. Hoje, em muitos casos, esses créditos são recuperados gradualmente ao longo de vários anos. “Uma indústria que faça um grande investimento, por exemplo em imóveis ou equipamentos, pode ficar meses ou até anos sem pagar CBS”, afirmou. Segundo Barreirinhas, isso ocorrerá porque os investimentos passarão a gerar créditos tributários de aproveitamento imediato, reduzindo o custo dos investimentos e a necessidade de manter recursos imobilizados à espera da recuperação tributária. O secretário também destacou a previsão de ressarcimento mais rápido dos créditos acumulados: “O ressarcimento, que hoje em dia demora, às vezes, até um ano para ser processado, vai ocorrer em 30, 60 ou 90 dias, a depender da conformidade desse empresário.” Ele lembrou ainda que o Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI) terá alíquota zerada para a maior parte dos produtos, permanecendo apenas em situações específicas destinadas à preservação da competitividade da Zona Franca de Manaus. Com informações de Agência Brasil Imagem: Envato O post Reforma tributária: governo apresentará texto para facilitar adaptação apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .
koreanSummary: O governo federal vai encaminhar ao Congresso Nacional uma proposta para criar uma regra de transição na cobrança da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), novo tributo federal da reforma tributária.

A medida permitirá que as empresas façam um cálculo estimado do imposto nos primeiros meses de vigência do sistema e realizem ajustes posteriormente, reduzindo dificuldades na adaptação às novas regras.

O anúncio foi feito nesta quarta-feira, 11, pelo secretário especial da Receita Federal , Robinson Barreirinhas, durante coletiva de imprensa sobre o Programa de Conformidade da Reforma Tributária, no Ministério da Fazenda.

PAR Technology Corporation, a leading technology provider powering multi-unit operators across restaurant, retail, and large-scale commerce, today announced that FSC Franchise Co. (“FSC”), franchisor of Beef ‘O’ Brady’s, The Brass Tap, and Newk’s Eatery, has selected PAR Punchh, PAR Ordering, and PAR Catering as its recommended solutions across its restaurant brands, creating a more connected technology foundation with PAR Intelligence, PAR’s agentic intelligence layer, built in. The announcement builds on the brands’ existing relationships with PAR Technology and represents the next step in FSC’s strategy to create a more connected technology foundation across its portfolio. By expanding its use of PAR solutions, FSC aims to better connect guest engagement, digital ordering, and catering while creating opportunities for more actionable insights into guest behavior and restaurant operations. “We’ve built Beef ’O’ Brady’s, The Brass Tap, and Newk’s Eatery into three distinct brands, each with its own identity and loyal following. But our franchisees shouldn’t have to navigate three different technology environments to operate their restaurants,” said Jason Saposnik, Vice President of Information Technology at FSC Franchise Co. “Standardizing on PAR gives our brands a stronger, more connected foundation for guest engagement, ordering, and catering. It helps simplify the technology experience for our franchisees and gives us the tools to continue improving how we serve our guests. PAR is the right partner at the right time for where FSC is headed.” “FSC has built three distinct brands with real followings, and the technology behind them should reflect that investment,” said Savneet Singh, CEO of PAR Technology. “When ordering, catering, and loyalty all run on the same platform across every brand, franchisees stop managing systems and start running restaurants. Every transaction feeds the same intelligence layer, every guest interaction gets smarter, and every new feature reaches all three brands at the same time. That’s what a unified platform means in practice, and that’s why brands are choosing to consolidate on PAR.” The transition will take place through a phased rollout beginning in early 2027, with each brand building on its existing PAR technology footprint: Newk’s Eatery, a fast-casual restaurant brand with more than 100 locations across 13 states, is already a PAR Punchh and PAR OPS customer. By adding PAR Ordering and PAR Catering, Newk’s is expanding its connected technology ecosystem across digital ordering, catering, and guest loyalty. The integration will help streamline the guest experience, support restaurant operations, and provide a stronger foundation for understanding guest engagement and encouraging repeat visits. Beef ’O’ Brady’s, a family-friendly sports pub concept with 125 locations across 15 states, already utilizes PAR Ordering, and PAR Punchh. By adding PAR Catering, the brand is extending its connected technology experience to catering orders and events. Bringing ordering, catering, and loyalty closer together will create a more seamless experience for guests while giving the brand a more complete view of customer engagement across channels. The Brass Tap, a Social House & Kitchen concept with 52 locations across 16 states, is adopting PAR Punchh to bring its loyalty program onto the same platform used by its sister brands. This move creates an opportunity to strengthen guest engagement, deliver more personalized rewards, and build consistency across FSC’s three restaurant concepts, while allowing each brand to maintain its own unique identity and guest experience.
